name_of_work: The Seafarer, Translated by Ezra Pound
content: May I for my own self song's truth reckon, Journey's jargon, how I in harsh days Hardship endured oft. Bitter breast-cares have I abided, Known on my keel many a care's hold, And dire sea-surge, and there I oft spent Narrow nightwatch nigh the ship's head While she tossed close to cliffs. Coldly afflicted, My feet were by frost benumbed. Chill its chains are; chafing sighs Hew my heart round and hunger begot Mere-weary mood. Lest man know not That he on dry land loveliest liveth, List how I, care-wretched, on ice-cold sea, Weathered the winter, wretched outcast Deprived of my kinsmen; Hung with hard ice-flakes, where hail-scur flew, There I heard naught save the harsh sea And ice-cold wave, at whiles the swan cries, Did for my games the gannet's clamour, Sea-fowls, loudness was for me laughter, The mews' singing all my mead-drink. Storms, on the stone-cliffs beaten, fell on the stern In icy feathers; full oft the eagle screamed With spray on his pinion. Not any protector May make merry man faring needy. This he little believes, who aye in winsome life Abides 'mid burghers some heavy business, Wealthy and wine-flushed, how I weary oft Must bide above brine. Neareth nightshade, snoweth from north, Frost froze the land, hail fell on earth then Corn of the coldest. Nathless there knocketh now The heart's thought that I on high streams The salt-wavy tumult traverse alone. Moaneth alway my mind's lust That I fare forth, that I afar hence Seek out a foreign fastness. For this there's no mood-lofty man over earth's midst, Not though he be given his good, but will have in his youth greed; Nor his deed to the daring, nor his king to the faithful But shall have his sorrow for sea-fare Whatever his lord will. He hath not heart for harping, nor in ring-having Nor winsomeness to wife, nor world's delight Nor any whit else save the wave's slash, Yet longing comes upon him to fare forth on the water. Bosque taketh blossom, cometh beauty of berries, Fields to fairness, land fares brisker, All this admonisheth man eager of mood, The heart turns to travel so that he then thinks On flood-ways to be far departing. Cuckoo calleth with gloomy crying, He singeth summerward, bodeth sorrow, The bitter heart's blood. Burgher knows not -- He the prosperous man -- what some perform Where wandering them widest draweth. So that but now my heart burst from my breast-lock, My mood 'mid the mere-flood, Over the whale's acre, would wander wide. On earth's shelter cometh oft to me, Eager and ready, the crying lone-flyer, Whets for the whale-path the heart irresistibly, O'er tracks of ocean; seeing that anyhow My lord deems to me this dead life On loan and on land, I believe not That any earth-weal eternal standeth Save there be somewhat calamitous That, ere a man's tide go, turn it to twain. Disease or oldness or sword-hate Beats out the breath from doom-gripped body. And for this, every earl whatever, for those speaking after -- Laud of the living, boasteth some last word, That he will work ere he pass onward, Frame on the fair earth 'gainst foes his malice, Daring ado, ... So that all men shall honour him after And his laud beyond them remain 'mid the English, Aye, for ever, a lasting life's-blast, Delight mid the doughty. Days little durable, And all arrogance of earthen riches, There come now no kings nor Caesars Nor gold-giving lords like those gone. Howe'er in mirth most magnified, Whoe'er lived in life most lordliest, Drear all this excellence, delights undurable! Waneth the watch, but the world holdeth. Tomb hideth trouble. The blade is layed low. Earthly glory ageth and seareth. No man at all going the earth's gait, But age fares against him, his face paleth, Grey-haired he groaneth, knows gone companions, Lordly men are to earth o'ergiven, Nor may he then the flesh-cover, whose life ceaseth, Nor eat the sweet nor feel the sorry, Nor stir hand nor think in mid heart, And though he strew the grave with gold, His born brothers, their buried bodies Be an unlikely treasure hoard.

These hills are sandy. Trees are dwarfed here. Crows Caw dismally in skies of an arid brilliance, Complain in dusty pine-trees. Yellow daybreak Lights on the long brown slopes a frost-like dew, Dew as heavy as rain; the rabbit tracks Show sharply in it, as they might in snow. But it's soon gone in the sun--what good does it do? The houses, on the slope, or among brown trees, Are grey and shrivelled. And the men who live here Are small and withered, spider-like, with large eyes. Bring water with you if you come to live here-- Cold tinkling cisterns, or else wells so deep That one looks down to Ganges or Himalayas. Yes, and bring mountains with you, white, moon-bearing, Mountains of ice. You will have need of these Profundities and peaks of wet and cold. Bring also, in a cage of wire or osier, Birds of a golden colour, who will sing Of leaves that do not wither, watery fruits That heavily hang on long melodious boughs In the blue-silver forests of deep valleys. I have now been here--how many years? Years unnumbered. My hands grow clawlike. My eyes are large and starved. I brought no bird with me, I have no cistern Where I might find the moon, or river, or snow. Some day, for lack of these, I'll spin a web Between two dusty pine-tree tops, and hang there Face downward, like a spider, blown as lightly As ghost of leaf. Crows will caw about me. Morning and evening I shall drink the dew.

The little girl loved to play in her garden. One day, she spotted something really special - a yellow flower! It was so bright and pretty, and it made her so happy.

The little girl asked her mom what it was called, and she said it was a sunflower. She told her to water it every day and soon it would bloom.

The little girl watched the sunflower every day and sure enough, one day it bloomed! She was so excited and ran to tell her mom.

Her mom said that the sunflower was so special that it was like medicine for her soul, and the little girl understood. She made sure to water and talk to the sunflower every day now.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big tent in the park. They want to go inside the tent.

"Can we go in the tent?" Anna asks Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe someone lives in the tent. We should be polite and ask first," Ben says.

They look around, but they do not see anyone. They walk to the tent and knock on the door.

"Hello? Is anyone there? Can we come in?" Anna calls.

There is no answer. Anna and Ben wait for a while, but nothing happens.

"Maybe no one is home. Let's go in and see what is inside," Anna says.

She opens the door and steps inside. Ben follows her. They see a lot of things in the tent. There are pillows, blankets, books, toys, and a lamp.

"Wow, this is a nice tent. It looks cozy and fun," Ben says.

He picks up a book and looks at the pictures. Anna sees a teddy bear on the bed. She likes teddy bears. She goes to the bed and hugs the teddy bear.

"Hello, teddy. You are so soft and cute. Can I be your friend?" Anna says.

She does not see the person hiding under the blanket. The person hears Anna and Ben. The person is not happy. The person does not like strangers in the tent. The person wants to scare them away.

The person jumps out of the blanket and shouts, "Surprise!"

Anna and Ben are very scared. They see a man with a beard and a hat. He looks angry and mean.

"Who are you? What are you doing in my tent? Get out of here!" the man yells.

He grabs the teddy bear from Anna and the book from Ben. He throws them on the floor.

Anna and Ben are sorry. They did not mean to make the man mad. They did not know he lived in the tent. They run out of the tent and back to the park.

They are sad and scared. They do not want to play in the tent anymore. They want to go home.

They learn a lesson. They learn to be polite and ask before they go into someone else's home. They learn to be careful and not to surprise people who do not like surprises. They learn to be respectful and not to touch things that do not belong to them. They learn to be friends and to help each other.

name_of_work: To Any Reader by Robert Louis Stevenson
content: As from the house your mother sees You playing round the garden trees, So you may see, if you will look Through the windows of this book, Another child, far, far away, And in another garden, play. But do not think you can at all, By knocking on the window, call That child to hear you. He intent Is all on his play-business bent. He does not hear; he will not look, Nor yet be lured out of this book. For, long ago, the truth to say, He has grown up and gone away, And it is but a child of air That lingers in the garden there.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play outside. But today the weather is bad. It is cold and wet and windy. They cannot go out.

They are sad and bored. They look at their toys. They do not want to play with them. They want to go out.

They have an idea. They can escape. They can go to the attic. The attic is a secret place. They can find old things and make stories.

They are quiet. They do not want Mom and Dad to hear them. They sneak up the stairs. They open the door. They go inside.

The attic is dark and dusty. But they see a window. They go to the window. They look outside. The sky is clear. The sun is shining. The weather is good.

They are happy. They smile. They escape. They go out.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Sam and Sue. Sam had a helmet that he wanted to decorate. Sue offered to help. First, Sue and Sam went to the store to look for sticker to put on Sam's helmet. Sam liked the cheap ones, so they got some of those.

They went back to Sam's house to decorate. Sam and Sue picked the best stickers and put them on the helmet. They put the stars on the top and the planets around the sides. They even made a picture in the middle!

When they were done, Sue and Sam looked at the helmet. It looked amazing! Now Sam had a cool helmet that was decorated just for him. He was very proud of it. The two friends went out to play wearing their helmets to show them off.

Once there was a friendly animal who lived in the forest. His name was Alli. Alli wanted to understand the world around him.

One day, Alli saw an open door in the forest. Alli wanted to know what was inside. He went closer to the door and looked inside. He only saw something harmless, like some leaves and a small animal. Alli was happy.

Alli wanted to know more. He pushed on the open door, and to his surprise it opened. Alli eagerly went inside. He saw many wonderful things he could not understand. As he looked around, he found something that he could understand - a friendly little bird.

The bird said â€œHello Alli! Welcome to my home. Would you like to stay and learn more about the forest?â€ Alli nodded happily.

The bird told Alli many things about the forest, and Alli began to understand the world around him. By the end of the day, Alli had a lot of new knowledge and understanding about the forest.

Jimmy was a happy little boy who loved to hop. Everywhere he went, Jimmy hopped and hopped. One day, Jimmy's parents bought him a bicycle and he was so excited!
Jimmy hopped around the bicycle and then hopped on. He peddled and peddled until he couldn't pedal anymore.
When Jimmy had finished, he hopped off and tidied up the bicycle. He made sure it was nice and tidy before he hopped away.
Jimmy loved his bike so much and he was so proud that he had kept it neatly organised. 
Jimmy continued to hop around and enjoy his new bike. Everywhere Jimmy went, he was hopping with a tidy bicycle!

Once upon a time, there was a snow day. All of the children were so excited to go outside and play in the snow. They ran outside and started to have fun. They threw snowballs and made snow angels in the soft, white snow.

The snow was so magical and playful. It seemed to jump around and make shapes. The sun was shining and everyone was happy.

Suddenly, the snow began to get very cold. All of the children knew that it was time to go inside and get warm. They all ran back inside, ready to lock the door against the snow.

Everyone felt safe and snug inside. They all had so much fun playing in the snow. They even decided to make a snowman in their backyard.

The snow changed everything. It was so magical and playful. Everyone enjoyed the snow day and no one wanted it to end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug named Billy. Billy was very alert. He liked to watch all the things around him. He saw the sun come up and the sun go down. He saw the birds fly and the fish swim.

One day, Billy saw a girl named Sally. Sally liked to write. She had a big book and a small pen. Billy watched Sally write in her book. He liked the way she made lines and circles. He wanted to write too.

Billy found a small stick. He used the stick to write in the dirt. He made lines and circles just like Sally. He was very happy. Now, Billy could write too. He wrote all day long, until the sun went down. And that is how Billy the alert bug learned to write.

name_of_work: To His Coy Mistress by Andrew Marvell
content: Had we but world enough and time, This coyness, lady, were no crime. We would sit down, and think which way To walk, and pass our long love's day. Thou by the Indian Ganges' side Shouldst rubies find; I by the tide Of Humber would complain. I would Love you ten years before the flood, And you should, if you please, refuse Till the conversion of the Jews. My vegetable love should grow Vaster than empires and more slow; An hundred years should go to praise Thine eyes, and on thy forehead gaze; Two hundred to adore each breast, But thirty thousand to the rest; An age at least to every part, And the last age should show your heart. For, lady, you deserve this state, Nor would I love at lower rate. But at my back I always hear Time's winged chariot hurrying near; And yonder all before us lie Deserts of vast eternity. Thy beauty shall no more be found; Nor, in thy marble vault, shall sound My echoing song; then worms shall try That long-preserved virginity, And your quaint honour turn to dust, And into ashes all my lust; The grave's a fine and private place, But none, I think, do there embrace. Now therefore, while the youthful hue Sits on thy skin like morning dew, And while thy willing soul transpires At every pore with instant fires, Now let us sport us while we may, And now, like amorous birds of prey, Rather at once our time devour Than languish in his slow-chapped power. Let us roll all our strength and all Our sweetness up into one ball, And tear our pleasures with rough strife Through the iron gates of life: Thus, though we cannot make our sun Stand still, yet we will make him run.

Once upon a time, there was a bear and a mouse. The bear was feeling lonely, so he went to the mouse's house to visit. The mouse was so happy to see the bear that he welcomed him in with a big hug.

The mouse offered the bear some tea in a special, unique cup. The cup was so colourful that the bear was filled with happiness. While they were chatting, the bear asked the mouse why he had such a special cup.

The mouse replied, "Every person is unique, like this cup! Always treat each person you meet with kindness, because everyone is special in their own way".

The bear was so glad to hear this message. He hugged the mouse again and thanked him for the cup of tea. From then on, the bear treated everyone he saw with respect and kindness, just like the mouse had said.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to wear pretty dresses and shiny shoes. One day, Lily went to visit her grandma. Her grandma gave her a cup of milk to drink. The cup was big and blue, and Lily held it with both hands. She drank all the milk and felt happy.

After that, Lily helped her grandma in the garden. They planted flowers and talked about the animals they saw. Lily saw a humble bee and said, "Look, grandma! A bee! It's humble." Her grandma smiled and said, "Yes, it is. Bees are important for the flowers." Lily felt proud that she learned a new word. She hugged her grandma and said goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. Mommy was walking in the park with her two children, Jimmy and Jenny. Jimmy and Jenny loved the park. They wanted to explore.

Mommy decided they should follow a special trail that had lots of exciting plants and animals. Jimmy and Jenny were so excited! They ran along the trail, exploring and playing.

Then, Mommy saw something very special. It was a baby rabbit, and it was running away. Mommy asked Jimmy and Jenny to help her catch it. 

Jimmy and Jenny were so excited. They followed the baby rabbit and tried to keep up. Finally, Jimmy was able to squeeze the baby rabbit right into his hands. 

But when Jenny saw this, she became very jealous. She wished that she could have caught the baby rabbit. 

Mommy saw Jenny's jealous face and hugged her. Mommy said, "Don't worry, there will be more trails and more rabbits for you to catch!â€

Jimmy and Jenny were so happy! They thanked Mommy and started running down the trail, following all the exciting things that they could find. 

THE

Tom and Mia like to play outside. They have a big yard with a slide, a swing and a ball. They like to run, jump and slide. They say it is good exercise.

One day, they see a big truck on the road. The truck is very loud and fast. It makes a lot of smoke and noise. Tom and Mia are curious. They want to see the truck better.

They run to the fence and look at the truck. The truck is red and shiny. It has a lot of wheels and a horn. The truck driver sees Tom and Mia. He waves at them and honks the horn. Tom and Mia wave back and laugh.

But then, they hear a voice. It is their mom. She is angry. She yells at them.

"Tom! Mia! Come back here right now! You know you are not allowed to go near the road! It is dangerous! The truck can hurt you!"

Tom and Mia are scared. They did not mean to make mom angry. They run back to the yard. They say sorry to mom.

Mom hugs them and says, "I know you were curious, but you have to be careful. The road is not a place to play. The truck can speed and hit you. You can play with your toys in the yard. That is safer and more fun."

Tom and Mia nod. They understand. They say they love mom. Mom says she loves them too. They go back to play with their toys. They forget about the truck. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was three years old. She was walking in the woods when she stumbled upon a mine. It was unknown how deep or how big it was. She decided to explore it.

She walked carefully down the dark tunnel. Suddenly, she smelled a yummy smell. She followed it until she found a big pile of apples. She was so happy! She ate as many apples as she could. 

But then, the little girl started feeling really tired. She fell asleep in the mine and dreamed of eating lots of delicious apples.

The next morning, the little girl woke up. She was still in the mine, and the apples were gone! She slowly walked back home, still dreaming of the mysterious, unknown apples she had eaten the night before.

She wanted a little room for thinking; but she saw diapers steaming on the line, a doll slumped behind the door. So she lugged a chair behind the garage to sit out the children's naps. Sometimes there were things to watch - the pinched armor of a vanished cricket, a floating maple leaf. Other days she stared until she was assured when she closed her eyes she'd see only her own vivid blood. She had an hour, at best, before Liza appeared pouting from the top of the stairs. And just what was mother doing out back with the field mice? Why, building a palace. Later that night when Thomas rolled over and lurched into her, she would open her eyes and think of the place that was hers for an hour - where she was nothing, pure nothing, in the middle of the day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She really wanted to succeed and make her mum and dad proud. So she went on a search. She looked everywhere, but there was no success. 

She was getting wet and tired, but then the little girl had an idea. She picked a flower and started to draw a sunshine with it. Suddenly the sun was in the sky, drying up the wet ground.

The little girl smiled, she had found success. She knew this would make her mum and dad proud. She quickly ran back home and showed them her work. 

The mum and dad smiled and hugged their little girl. The search was a success!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys, especially her dolls. One day, her mom took her to the toy store. Lily was so happy and excited to see all the toys in the store.

She looked around and saw many dolls, teddy bears, and other toys. She wanted to buy everything, but her mom told her she could only choose one toy. Lily felt sad because she couldn't have everything she wanted.

After looking at all the toys, Lily finally chose a beautiful figure of a princess. She felt so happy and proud of her choice. When they got home, Lily played with her new toy and felt very happy.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we can't have everything we want, but we can still be happy with the things we choose. Lily was tired of wanting everything, but she learned that choosing one thing can make her just as happy.

Lily was a small cat who liked to hide. She hid under the bed, behind the sofa, and in the closet. She hid from her owner, Tom, who was a large boy. Tom loved Lily, but he sometimes played too rough with her. He liked to chase her, hug her, and dress her up.

One day, Tom came home with a new toy. It was a big, noisy truck that made loud sounds and flashed bright lights. Tom was very happy and wanted to show Lily his truck. He looked for her in all her hiding places, but he could not find her. He called her name, but she did not answer.

Lily was hiding in a new place. She had found a small hole in the wall behind the bookshelf. She crawled inside and felt safe and cozy. She could hear Tom's truck, but she did not want to come out. She thought Tom would make her play with his truck, and she did not like it.

Tom was sad and worried. He missed Lily and wondered where she was. He asked his mom and dad, but they did not know. He looked everywhere, but he could not see her. He wished Lily would come back and play with him.

Lily heard Tom's voice. She heard him say he was sorry and he loved her. She felt sorry for Tom. She realized he was lonely and he just wanted to have fun. She decided to come out of her hiding place and surprise him. She poked her head out of the hole and meowed.

Tom heard Lily's meow. He turned around and saw her. He was very happy and ran to her. He hugged her gently and thanked her for coming back. He told her he had a new toy, but he did not have to play with it if she did not like it. He asked her what she wanted to do.

Lily purred and licked his face. She wanted to play with Tom, but not with his truck. She wanted to play hide and seek. She ran away and hid under the bed. Tom smiled and followed her. He counted to ten and then looked for her. They played for a long time and had fun. They were both happy.

Sara and Tom were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a shiny thing in the grass. It was a gem that someone had lost. Sara wanted to keep it, but Tom said they should give it back.

"Whoever lost this gem must be very sad," Tom said. "We should find them and make them happy."

"But it is so pretty," Sara said. "I want to have it. It is mine now."

She put the gem in her pocket and ran away. Tom followed her, but he was angry.

Sara ran to her house and showed the gem to her mom. Her mom was surprised and asked her where she got it.

"I found it in the park," Sara said. "It is mine."

Her mom shook her head. "No, Sara, it is not yours. It belongs to someone else. You should not take things that are not yours. That is wrong. You should be sorry and return it."

Sara felt bad. She knew her mom was right. She had been foolish and greedy. She had hurt her friend and the owner of the gem. She regretted what she had done.

She took the gem and ran back to the park. She hoped Tom was still there. She wanted to say sorry and give the gem back.

She saw Tom sitting on a bench. He looked sad. She ran to him and held out the gem.

"Tom, I am sorry," she said. "I was wrong. I should not have taken the gem. It is not mine. Can you forgive me?"

Tom looked at her and smiled. He took the gem and hugged her.

"Of course I forgive you, Sara," he said. "You are my friend. I am glad you came back. Let's go and find the owner of the gem. Maybe they are still looking for it."

They held hands and walked around the park. They saw a lady crying on a bench. She had a necklace with a hole where the gem used to be.

"Excuse me, lady," Tom said. "Is this your gem?"

He showed her the gem. The lady gasped and smiled. She took the gem and thanked them.

"You are very kind and honest, children," she said. "You have made me very happy. This gem was a gift from my husband. He is gone now, but this gem reminds me of him. I was so sad when I lost it. Thank you for bringing it back."

She gave them each a hug and a candy. Sara and Tom felt happy too. They had done the right thing. They had learned a lesson. They had been good friends.

name_of_work: Sudden Light by Dante Gabriel Rossetti
content: I have been here before, But when or how I cannot tell: I know the grass beyond the door, The sweet keen smell, The sighing sound, the lights around the shore. You have been mine before,-- How long ago I may not know: But just when at that swallow's soar Your neck turn'd so, Some veil did fall,--I knew it all of yore. Has this been thus before? And shall not thus time's eddying flight Still with our lives our love restore In death's despite, And day and night yield one delight once more?

name_of_work: Hard Rock Returns to Prison by Etheridge Knight
content: Hard Rock / was / "known not to take no shit From nobody," and he had the scars to prove it: Split purple lips, lumbed ears, welts above His yellow eyes, and one long scar that cut Across his temple and plowed through a thick Canopy of kinky hair. The WORD / was / that Hard Rock wasn't a mean nigger Anymore, that the doctors had bored a hole in his head, Cut out part of his brain, and shot electricity Through the rest. When they brought Hard Rock back, Handcuffed and chained, he was turned loose, Like a freshly gelded stallion, to try his new status. And we all waited and watched, like a herd of sheep, To see if the WORD was true. As we waited we wrapped ourselves in the cloak Of his exploits: "Man, the last time, it took eight Screws to put him in the Hole." "Yeah, remember when he Smacked the captain with his dinner tray?" "He set The record for time in the Hole--67 straight days!" "Ol Hard Rock! man, that's one crazy nigger." And then the jewel of a myth that Hard Rock had once bit A screw on the thumb and poisoned him with syphilitic spit. The testing came, to see if Hard Rock was really tame. A hillbilly called him a black son of a bitch And didn't lose his teeth, a screw who knew Hard Rock From before shook him down and barked in his face. And Hard Rock did nothing. Just grinned and looked silly, His eyes empty like knot holes in a fence. And even after we discovered that it took Hard Rock Exactly 3 minutes to tell you his first name, We told ourselves that he had just wised up, Was being cool; but we could not fool ourselves for long, And we turned away, our eyes on the ground. Crushed. He had been our Destroyer, the doer of things We dreamed of doing but could not bring ourselves to do, The fears of years, like a biting whip, Had cut deep bloody grooves Across our backs.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went outside to collect pretty rocks. She had a big bag to put them in. She loved her rocks very much.

While Lucy was looking for rocks, she saw a small bird on the ground. The bird looked sad and hurt. Lucy knew this was an emergency. She wanted to help the bird, so she ran to her mom.

"Mom, there is a hurt bird outside! We need to help it!" said Lucy. Her mom was very generous and kind. She knew what to do. They got a box and a soft towel to make the bird feel better.

Lucy and her mom went outside and gently put the bird in the box. They took it to a nice man who helped animals. The bird got better and flew away. Lucy was happy that she could help the bird and went back to collecting her pretty rocks.

name_of_work: Adam and Eve by Marjorie Pickthall
content: When the first dark had fallen around them And the leaves were weary of praise, In the clear silence Beauty found them And shewed them all her ways. In the high noon of the heavenly garden Where the angels sunned with the birds, Beauty, before their hearts could harden, Had taught them heavenly words. When they fled in the burning weather And nothing dawned but a dream, Beauty fasted their hands together And cooled them at her stream. And when day wearied and night grew stronger, And they slept as the beautiful must, Then she bided a little longer, And blossomed from their dust.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she saw a new girl named Sarah in the park. Lily wanted to be friends with Sarah, so she went over to introduce herself. Sarah was happy to meet Lily and they became friends.

A few days later, Lily and Sarah went to the store to buy a basket for their picnic. They found a cheap basket that was perfect for carrying their sandwiches and drinks. They were so excited to use it for their picnic in the park.

At the park, they spread out their blanket and put the basket in the middle. They had a great time eating their sandwiches and playing games. Lily was happy that she introduced herself to Sarah and made a new friend. From that day on, they had many more picnics together with their cheap basket.

Anne was very excited. She had a big box of tubes. She gathered them all up in her room and started to organize them. She stacked some of the tubes in a wall and the others she put in a circle in the middle of the room.

Anne went to look out her window. It was cold outside, so she decided to stay inside and keep organizing her tubes. She moved the tubes in the circle around until they fit together like a puzzle. She was so proud of her work.

Anne enjoyed organizing the tubes so much she decided to bring the box outside. She ran to the garden and spread the tubes out on the grass. She arranged them into many different shapes. She created spirals and triangles and circles.

Finally, Anne was done. She was proud of the shapes and structures she had made. She wanted to show everyone what she had done so she gathered up all the tubes and put them back in the box. She couldnâ€™t wait to show everyone her project!

Gumtree in the city street, Hard bitumen around your feet, Rather you should be In the cool world of leafy forest halls And wild bird calls Here you seems to me Like that poor cart-horse Castrated, broken, a thing wronged, Strapped and buckled, its hell prolonged, Whose hung head and listless mien express Its hopelessness. Municipal gum, it is dolorous To see you thus Set in your black grass of bitumen-- O fellow citizen, What have they done to us?

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved eating sugar and playing with her toys. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. While playing, she met a new friend named Jack. Jack was a big dog who was very friendly. Lily was frightened at first, but Jack was nice and made her feel safe.

Lily and Jack played together for a while and had a lot of fun. They even shared some sugar that Lily had brought with her. Suddenly, Jack saw a cat and ran after it. Lily tried to stop him, but Jack was too fast. He chased the cat across the street and got hit by a car. Lily was very sad and cried a lot.

Lily's mom came to pick her up and saw what had happened. She hugged Lily and told her that Jack had gone to a better place. Lily was still sad, but she knew that Jack was happy now. She went home and hugged her toys, feeling grateful for the time she had spent with Jack.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to hop on the grass and look for bugs. They saw a big light in the sky. It was the sun.

"Look, the sun is so bright!" Lily said.

"I want to touch it!" Ben said.

He tried to hop higher and higher, but he could not reach the sun. He got angry.

"That's silly, Ben. You can't touch the sun. It's too far and too hot," Lily said.

"Yes, I can! You are mean!" Ben said.

He pushed Lily and made her fall. She started to cry.

"Ben, why did you do that?" Lily asked.

"Because you are not my friend!" Ben said.

He ran away from Lily and the sun. He felt sad and lonely.

Lily got up and wiped her tears. She saw a lady walking a dog. The dog was fluffy and friendly. It licked Lily's face and made her smile.

"Hello, little girl. Do you like my dog?" the lady asked.

"Yes, I do. He is very nice," Lily said.

"His name is Spot. Do you want to pet him?" the lady asked.

"Yes, please," Lily said.

She petted Spot and felt happy. She forgot about Ben and the sun.

"Maybe Ben will come back and say sorry," Lily thought.

"Maybe he will learn to share and be kind," Lily hoped.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to brush her hair with a pink brush. Her brush was very pretty and had sparkles on it. She would brush her hair every day and it would be very smooth.

One day, Lily was brushing her hair very loudly. Her mom told her to be quiet because her little brother was sleeping. But Lily didn't listen and kept brushing her hair loudly.

Suddenly, her little brother woke up and started crying. He was scared because the loud noise woke him up. Lily felt very bad and tried to make him feel better. She gave him a hug and said sorry.

From that day on, Lily always remembered to be quiet when her brother was sleeping. She still loved to brush her hair with her pretty pink brush, but she made sure to do it quietly.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. Jack was not very big, but he wanted to be a hero. Jack had a sword. The sword was not heavy. It was easy for Jack to hold.

One day, Jack saw a big dragon. Jack wanted to save the town from the dragon. Jack tried to fight the dragon with his sword. Jack thought it would be easy to win, but the dragon was very strong.

Jack did not succeed. The dragon was too big and too strong for Jack. Jack was sad that he could not save the town. The town was not safe, and the people were sad too.

Once upon a time there was a bear who needed a new pair of boots. He went to the store, but nothing there was big enough for his big feet. 

The storekeeper saw the bear looking sad and said, "I have something available for you!" 

The bear looked up excitedly. "Do you?" 

The storekeeper smiled. "Yes," he said, "I have one pair of extra-large boots. I can wrap them up and you can take them home." 

The bear was so happy he hugged the storekeeper. "Thank you, thank you," he said. 

The storekeeper laughed and said, "You're very welcome. Have a nice walk home in your new boots!" 

The bear grinned and happily skipped out of the store wearing his new boots. 

The end.

name_of_work: Clouds at Evening by Robinson Jeffers
content: Enormous cloud-mountains that form over Point Lobos and into the sunset, Figures of fire on the walls of to-night's storm, Foam of gold in gorges of fire, and the great file of warrior angels: Dreams gathering in the curded brain of the earth, The sky the brain-vault, on the threshold of sleep: poor earth, you like your children By mordinate desires tortured make dreams? Storms more enormous, wars nobler, more toppling mountains, more jewelled waters, more free Fires on impossible headlands ... as a poor girl Wishing her lover taller and more desirous, and herself maned with gold, Dreams the world right, in the cold bed, about dawn. Dreams are beautiful; the slaves of form are beautiful also; I have grown to believe A stone is a better pillow than many visions.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play pretend with her toys. One day, she pretended to be a princess and her teddy bear was her loyal servant. They had so much fun together.

But then, Lily got into trouble. She accidentally knocked over a vase and it broke into a million pieces. She felt very sorry and didn't know what to do. She knew she shouldn't have been playing so rough in the house.

Lily's mom came in and saw the broken vase. She was very angry and upset. Lily tried to explain that it was just an accident, but her mom didn't believe her. Lily was sent to her room and wasn't allowed to play with her toys for a long time.

Lily felt very sad and alone. She wished she could go back in time and not pretend to be a princess. She learned that sometimes pretending can lead to trouble and it's important to be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet was very noisy and liked to sing all day long. One day, Tweet saw a big bird soaring high in the sky. Tweet wanted to soar too, but didn't know how. 

Tweet asked the big bird how to soar and the big bird replied, "You need to have a strong spirit and believe in yourself." Tweet didn't understand what the big bird meant, but decided to try anyway. 

Tweet practiced flying every day and didn't give up. Soon, Tweet's spirit grew stronger and stronger. One day, Tweet soared high in the sky just like the big bird. Tweet was very happy and proud of themselves. 

The moral of the story is that if you believe in yourself and never give up, you can achieve anything you want.

name_of_work: To Her Father with Some Verses by Anne Bradstreet
content: Most truly honoured, and as truly dear, If worth in me or ought I do appear, Who can of right better demand the same Than may your worthy self from whom it came? The principal might yield a greater sum, Yet handled ill, amounts but to this crumb; My stock's so small I know not how to pay, My bond remains in force unto this day; Yet for part payment take this simple mite, Where nothing's to be had, kings loose their right. Such is my debt I may not say forgive, But as I can, I'll pay it while I live; Such is my bond, none can discharge but I, Yet paying is not paid until I die.

Once upon a time, there was a nice rocket. The rocket was so shiny and colorful! It made everyone so happy. One day, the rocket wanted to try something new. So it kneeled down on the ground and closed its eyes. It said a silent prayer.

After it was finished, the rocket opened its eyes and felt very content. Just then, it saw something tasty: a big red apple! The rocket couldn't believe it! So quickly, it grabbed the apple and went off to eat it. 

It was the most delicious apple that the rocket had ever tasted. It knew that it was going to be a special day. So the rocket gave a happy little dance and flew off into the sky, ready for more adventure.

name_of_work: On the Sonnet by John Keats
content: If by dull rhymes our English must be chain'd, And, like Andromeda, the Sonnet sweet Fetter'd, in spite of pained loveliness; Let us find out, if we must be constrain'd, Sandals more interwoven and complete To fit the naked foot of poesy; Let us inspect the lyre, and weigh the stress Of every chord, and see what may be gain'd By ear industrious, and attention meet: Misers of sound and syllable, no less Than Midas of his coinage, let us be Jealous of dead leaves in the bay wreath crown; So, if we may not let the Muse be free, She will be bound with garlands of her own.

Lily likes to write. She has a big book and a red pen. She writes about her toys, her friends and her cat. She writes every day.

One day, she sees a bug on her book. It is small and green. It has six legs and two wings. Lily thinks it is cute. She says, "Hello, bug. Do you want to be my friend?"

The bug does not say anything. It crawls on her book. It makes a hole in her page. Lily is sad. She says, "No, bug. You are not my friend. You are bad. You ruined my book."

The bug flies away. Lily cries. She hugs her book. She says, "I'm sorry, book. I love you. You are my best friend."

Her mom hears her cry. She comes to her room. She sees the hole in her book. She says, "What happened, Lily?"

Lily tells her mom about the bug. She says, "The bug was mean. It hurt my book. I don't like bugs."

Her mom hugs her. She says, "I'm sorry, Lily. Bugs can be naughty sometimes. But they don't mean to hurt you. They are just looking for food and a home. Maybe the bug liked your book too."

Lily thinks for a moment. She says, "Maybe. But I don't want to share my book with bugs. They can have other things. Like leaves and flowers."

Her mom smiles. She says, "That's very kind of you, Lily. How about we fix your book? We can use some tape and stickers. And we can write a new story together. What do you think?"

Lily smiles too. She says, "Yes, mom. That sounds fun. Thank you. I love you."

They hug and kiss. They fix the book. They write a new story. It is about Lily and her book and their adventures. They are happy.

name_of_work: I Love You by Ella Wheeler Wilcox
content: I love your lips when they're wet with wine And red with a wild desire; I love your eyes when the lovelight lies Lit with a passionate fire. I love your arms when the warm white flesh Touches mine in a fond embrace; I love your hair when the strands enmesh Your kisses against my face. Not for me the cold, calm kiss Of a virgin's bloodless love; Not for me the saint's white bliss, Nor the heart of a spotless dove. But give me the love that so freely gives And laughs at the whole world's blame, With your body so young and warm in my arms, It sets my poor heart aflame. So kiss me sweet with your warm wet mouth, Still fragrant with ruby wine, And say with a fervor born of the South That your body and soul are mine. Clasp me close in your warm young arms, While the pale stars shine above, And we'll live our whole young lives away In the joys of a living love.

Once upon a time there was a little cricket. He liked to march around all day. He went up and down the garden with a happy song in his heart.

One day, he heard a noise and stopped. There was a big, strong dog, barking and growling. The cricket was scared and ran away.

He ran and ran until he came to a friendly, old man. The man welcomed the cricket in and offered him dinner. The cricket told the old man his story and the old man was so kind. He gave the cricket a pair of boots. He said they were very useful.

The cricket put on the boots and started to march. He was so proud of his new marching boots. He forgot all about the scary dog. He thanked the old man, then marched off into the sunset.

Lily and Tom are brother and sister. They like to play together. One day, they go to the beach with their mom and dad. The beach is big and sandy. The water is blue and clear. Lily and Tom see many fish and shells.

"Look, Tom, a starfish!" Lily says. She picks up the starfish and shows it to Tom. "It is pretty and spiky."

"Wow, Lily, it is!" Tom says. He touches the starfish gently. "Can we keep it?"

"No, Tom, we have to put it back in the water. It is its home. We can find another one later." Lily says. She puts the starfish back in the water and waves to it. "Bye, starfish!"

Lily and Tom play more on the beach. They make a sandcastle and a moat. They splash in the water and chase the waves. They have a lot of fun. They are happy.

When it is time to go home, Lily and Tom are tired. They get in the car with their mom and dad. They fall asleep on the way. They dream of the beach and the starfish. They smile in their sleep. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers. The older brother, Alex, was very stubborn. He did not like to listen to his parents and often ignored them. One day, the parents decided it was time for Alex to learn a lesson, so they punished him.

Alex was told he was not allowed to play his favourite video game for the whole day. Alex was very unhappy and he had an idea. He thought he could try to climb the wall in his garden and take the game from his parents' room.

The next day, Alex tried again and again to climb the wall but it was too difficult. After trying many times, he finally gave up. He realized it was wrong to disobey his parents and waste his time with something that was impossible. He accepted his punishment and learned his lesson. 

The moral of this story is that it is important to listen to your parents and accept the consequences of your actions. Being stubborn will not help you get what you want and it will only lead to wasted time and effort that could be better spent elsewhere.

One day, a little girl was walking in the park when she saw a funny animal. She stopped and said "Hello!" to it. The animal looked alert and it answered back. They began to talk and the little girl asked the animal what its name was. The animal said its name was Sammy. 

Sammy asked the little girl what her name was, and she said it was Lily. Lily and Sammy became very good friends and sometimes Sammy even sat on Lily's shoulder. They felt very comfortable with each other because Sammy was so alert and attentive while they talked.

Lily and Sammy talked and talked until it was time for Lily to go home. Before she left, Lily gave Sammy a big hug and said "Goodbye". Sammy waved goodbye as Lily walked away, and they both looked forward to the next time they would meet in the park.

Sara and Tom like to fish with Dad. They go to the lake and sit on the boat. Dad gives them a hook and a worm. He shows them how to put the worm on the hook and throw the line in the water.

"Be careful with the hook," Dad says. "It is sharp and can hurt you."

Sara and Tom nod. They wait for a fish to bite. They look at the water and the sky. They see ducks and birds. They hear frogs and crickets.

"Look, I got one!" Tom says. He feels a tug on his line. He pulls hard and reels in a big fish. It is shiny and wet. It flips and flops on the boat.

"Wow, good job, Tom!" Dad says. He helps Tom take the fish off the hook. He puts it in a bucket with water.

"Can I keep it?" Tom asks.

"Sure, you can keep it," Dad says. "But you have to take care of it. You have to feed it and change the water."

"OK, I will," Tom says. He is happy. He hugs his fish.

Sara wants to catch a fish too. She throws her line in the water again. She hopes a fish will bite. She thinks fish are fun and pretty.

"Maybe you will catch one too, Sara," Dad says. "You just have to be patient and quiet."

Sara nods. She is patient and quiet. She feels safe and happy on the boat with Dad and Tom. She likes to fish with them. She smiles.

Once upon a time, there was a polite little girl named Lily who lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, her mommy told her to be careful because there was a thief in the neighborhood who liked to steal things. Lily didn't know what a thief was, but she knew it was something bad.

The next day, Lily saw a strange man walking down the street. He looked like a thief to her. She remembered what her mommy had said and ran inside to tell her. Her mommy thanked her for being so observant and told her to stay inside where it was safe.

Days went by and nothing happened. Lily forgot about the thief and went back to playing with her dolls. But one day, her mommy told her that the thief had struck again. He had stolen some things from their neighbor's house. Lily was scared and didn't want the thief to come to her house.

So, she decided to increase the security around her house. She asked her daddy to put locks on all the doors and windows. Her mommy even got a big dog to scare away any bad guys. Lily felt safe again and knew she had done her part to keep her family and home protected.

And when I take them out of the cherrywood box these beads are the colour of dog-violets in shadow. Then at the well of the throat where tears start they darken. Now I wear at my neck an old stress of crystal: an impression of earthly housekeeping. A mysterious brightness made underground where there is no sun only stories of a strayed child and her mother bargaining with a sullen king. Promising and arguing: what she can keep, what she can let him have. Shadows and the season violets start up in are part of the settlement. Stolen from such a place these beads cannot be anything but wise to the healing arts of compromise, of survival. And when I wear them it is almost as if my skin was taking into itself a medicine of light. Something like the old simples. Rosemary, say, or tansy. Or camomile which they kept to cool fever. Which they once used to soothe a child tossing from side to side, beads of sweat catching and holding a gleam from the vigil lamp. A child crying out in her sleep Wait for me. Don't leave me here. Who will never remember this. Who will never remember this.

Once upon a time, there was a little tiger. He had powerful legs and could run very fast. He wanted to reach the highest hill in the forest. On the top of the hill, the tiger could see clearly over all the trees and the other animals.

The tiger ran up the hill, faster and faster. His legs moved quickly and he felt strong. Finally he reached the top. He stopped and saw how beautiful his forest was. He was so happy!

The tiger ran back down the hill and played with his friends. He showed them the clear view he had seen when he reached the top. They were very impressed.

Every day the tiger would reach the highest hill to see the view. He was very proud and strong. He felt like he was the king of the forest and the tigers were his loyal subjects.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read novels, especially ones about princesses and knights. One day, Lily went outside to play in the snow. It was very icy and she slipped and fell down.

Her friend, Timmy, saw her fall and ran over to help. "Are you okay, Lily?" he asked. Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I'm okay. I just slipped on the icy snow."

Timmy smiled back and said, "Let's go inside and read a novel together." Lily was very happy and they went inside to read their favorite story about a brave knight who saved a princess from a dragon. They laughed and smiled as they read the story together. From that day on, Lily and Timmy were the best of friends and loved to read novels and play in the snow together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She liked to read books every day. Every week, she would go to the library and take out new books.

One day, Lucy heard about a special festival. She was so excited and wanted to go! She asked her mom if she could go.

When the festival came, Lucy and her mom went there. There were so many fun things to do! Lucy read a story and tried many healthy foods. She even made some friends with the other kids there.

At the end of the day, Lucy was very tired, but she had so much fun at the festival. She couldn't wait to go back the next year!

Sorting out letters and piles of my old Canceled checks, old clippings, and yellow note cards That meant something once, I happened to find Your picture. That picture. I stopped there cold, Like a man raking piles of dead leaves in his yard Who has turned up a severed hand. Still, that first second, I was glad: you stand Just as you stood--shy, delicate, slender, In that long gown of green lace netting and daisies That you wore to our first dance. The sight of you stunned Us all. Well, our needs were different, then, And our ideals came easy. Then through the war and those two long years Overseas, the Japanese dead in their shacks Among dishes, dolls, and lost shoes; I carried This glimpse of you, there, to choke down my fear, Prove it had been, that it might come back. That was before we got married. --Before we drained out one another's force With lies, self-denial, unspoken regret And the sick eyes that blame; before the divorce And the treachery. Say it: before we met. Still, I put back your picture. Someday, in due course, I will find that it's still there.

One day, Linda went to the park with her mommy. Linda was very curious. She wanted to explore everywhere.

As they walked along the path, Linda noticed a piece of paper on the ground. Mommy said it was a note. Linda picked it up and put it in her pocket.

When it was time for Linda to go home, Mommy said they had to delay. Linda did not understand. But Mommy explained that they would have to wait a bit before they could go.

Linda waited patiently until it was time to go home. She was still very curious about the note, so she asked Mommy if they could look at it.

Mommy said they could, so Linda opened the note. It said, "Have a great day!" Linda smiled and put the note in her pocket again. Then she and Mommy went home.

name_of_work: From the Dark Tower by Countee Cullen
content: We shall not always plant while others reap The golden increment of bursting fruit, Not always countenance, abject and mute, That lesser men should hold their brothers cheap; Not everlastingly while others sleep Shall we beguile their limbs with mellow flute, Not always bend to some more subtle brute; We were not made to eternally weep. The night whose sable breast relieves the stark, White stars is no less lovely being dark, And there are buds that cannot bloom at all In light, but crumple, piteous, and fall; So in the dark we hide the heart that bleeds, And wait, and tend our agonizing seeds.

Once there was a little boy named Joe. He loved to look at all the shiny ornaments in his mom's closet. He always wanted to choose one of them to take with him wherever he went.

One day his mom said he could choose one of the ornaments to keep. He got so excited and quickly grabbed the biggest and shiniest ornament. His mom reminded him that he had to share it with his brothers and sisters.

Joe didn't want to share the ornament, so he quickly hid it in his bedroom. He pretended that he had forgotten about it and said he didn't want it after all. His mom was angry because he was being so selfish.

The next day Joe felt really bad about being so selfish. He knew the ornament would be a lot more fun if he shared it with others. So he decided to take it out of his bedroom, and give it to his dad for a present.

Joe's dad was so happy and proud of Joe for being so generous. Joe was glad he had chose to be kind instead of selfish.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a big parent who was always busy with work. One day, Timmy wanted to play with his parent, but they were too heavy to carry around. Timmy felt sad and regretted not playing with them earlier. 

That night, Timmy had a dream where his toys came to life and played with him. They had so much fun together! When Timmy woke up, he realized that he didn't need his heavy parent to have fun. He could play with his toys and be happy. Timmy promised himself that he wouldn't regret not playing with his toys anymore. 

From that day on, Timmy played with his toys every day and never felt lonely again. He loved his parent, but he knew that he could have fun on his own too. Timmy was happy and never regretted his decision to play with his toys.

Once upon a time there was a bear named Bill. Bill was very loyal to his friends. He liked to explore the forest looking for adventures. 

One day Bill was running through the forest when he stumbled across a huge vine. It was towering above him, so tall he couldn't reach the top! Bill started to climb the vine because he wanted to see what was at the top.

Once he reached the top, he found the most beautiful view. He was so happy he started to dance. Suddenly he heard a voice saying, "What are you doing up there?â€ 

It was Sam the owl. Sam had woken up early to see the sun come up and saw Bill dancing. Bill told him how he had climbed the vine to see the view. Sam laughed and said, â€œYou are so loyal and brave, Bill. Come back and visit me anytime.â€ 

Bill thanked Sam and ran back to the village to tell all his friends the great adventure he had just been on. Everyone was so impressed they decided they would all climb the vine the next day to see the sun come up. 

And from then on, the bear and the owl became the best of friends!

name_of_work: To a Lady that Desired I Would Love Her by Thomas Carew
content: Now you have freely given me leave to love, What will you do? Shall I your mirth, or passion move, When I begin to woo; Will you torment, or scorn, or love me too? Each petty beauty can disdain, and I Spite of your hate Without your leave can see, and die; Dispense a nobler fate! 'Tis easy to destroy, you may create. Then give me leave to love, and love me too Not with design To raise, as Love's cursed rebels do, When puling poets whine, Fame to their beauty, from their blubbered eyne. Grief is a puddle, and reflects not clear Your beauty's rays; Joys are pure streams, your eyes appear Sullen in sadder lays; In cheerful numbers they shine bright with praise, Which shall not mention to express you fair, Wounds, flames, and darts, Storms in your brow, nets in your hair, Suborning all your parts, Or to betray, or torture captive hearts. I'll make your eyes like morning suns appear, As mild, and fair; Your brow as crystal smooth, and clear, And your disheveled hair Shall flow like a calm region of the air.

name_of_work: 'Had I not been awake' by Seamus Heaney
content: Had I not been awake I would have missed it, A wind that rose and whirled until the roof Pattered with quick leaves off the sycamore And got me up, the whole of me a-patter, Alive and ticking like an electric fence: Had I not been awake I would have missed it It came and went too unexpectedly And almost it seemed dangerously, Hurtling like an animal at the house, A courier blast that there and then Lapsed ordinary. But not ever After. And not now.

Tom and Lily wanted to build a big tower with their blocks. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. They put the blocks on top of each other, one by one, until the tower was very tall.

"Look at our tower!" Tom said. "It is taller than me!"

Lily nodded. "It is taller than you and me and the chair and the lamp!" She said. "It is the tallest tower ever!"

They were very happy and proud of their tower. They wanted to show it to their mom and dad. But then, something bad happened. A big dog came into the room. The dog saw the tower and wanted to play with it. He ran towards the tower and jumped on it. The blocks fell down and made a loud noise.

"Hey!" Tom shouted. "Bad dog! You broke our tower!"

Lily started to cry. "Our tower is gone!" She said. "We worked so hard to build it!"

The dog looked at them with his big eyes and his wet nose. He wagged his tail and licked their faces. He did not know he did something wrong. He just wanted to have fun.

Tom and Lily were angry and sad at first. But then they saw the dog was sorry and friendly. They decided to forgive him and pet him. They also decided to build another tower, but this time in a different room, where the dog could not reach it. They hoped their mom and dad would see their tower and like it. They also hoped the dog would not break it again.

Dave was feeling gloomy. He had to go to the beach to find a seal his mommy missed. Dave put on his swimsuit and ran to the shore. He looked around and saw an old man.

"Have you seen a seal?", he asked the old man.

"Yes, my boy," the old man answered. "I have seen many seals near the rocks over there."

Dave thanked the old man and ran to the rocks. Sure enough, he could see a large seal bobbing in the waves. Dave smiled and waded out to greet the seal.

He held out his hand and said "Hello! My mommy misses you. Come with me and I will take you home."

The seal slowly swam over to Dave, and he followed him back to shore. Dave held the seal close and walked home happily. When Dave and the seal arrived home, his mommy was waiting for them. "Thank you, Dave!" she said, and gave him a big hug.

Dave was glad he could make his mommy happy. From then on, Dave went back to the beach every day to make sure the seal was still there. He enjoyed spending time with the seal, and his mommy never missed it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the museum with her mommy and daddy. They would look at all the pretty paintings and sculptures.

One day, when they went to the museum, Lily saw a lovely necklace in a glass case. She really wanted to touch it, but her mommy said no. Lily got very upset and started to cry. Her mommy explained that it was not allowed to touch anything in the museum.

Lily was sad, but then her daddy let her take a picture of the necklace. She felt better and they continued to enjoy the rest of the museum. From that day on, Lily knew that even though she couldn't touch everything, she could still enjoy looking at all the lovely things in the museum.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mabel. She was 3 years old and loved to pretend.

One day, Mabel went for lunch with her mom. They saw a menu with orange and other colors on it.

Mabel asked her mom, "Can we pretend to eat the things on the menu?"

Mom smiled and nodded.

So Mabel and her mom pretended to eat big, juicy oranges. They pretended to bite through their thick skin and enjoy their sweet juice.

Mabel and her mom pretended they were having so much fun that they almost forgot it was only pretend.

And when they were done pretending, they both had the biggest smiles on their faces!

Once upon a time there was a cute monkey named Bobo. Bobo loved to swing from tree to tree and explore the jungle with his friends.

One day Bobo fell off a tree and hurt his arm. His friends knew his arm was hurt and took him to get an x-ray. Bobo was scared at first, but then he saw the x-ray machine and thought it was cool. He smiled when his friends explained what the machine does and he felt better.

But when the x-ray results came back, Bobo's friends told him he had to stay in bed for a few days and be careful. Bobo was sad because he couldn't go out and play.

One day, Bobo's friends came over with some new games they'd made and they helped him get better. Bobo was so happy and felt like he was making progress. Finally, Bobo finished playing with the games and he felt great. He was ready to explore the jungle again!

One day, two friends decided to go for a walk. As they were walking, they saw a piece of paper in the street, which made them wonder what it was for.

So, the two friends decided to pick it up to take a closer look. When they opened it, they found that it had some crazy words written on it.

The two friends didn't know what it meant, so they decided to keep it to show Grandma. Grandma knew a lot more than they did and they wanted to know what the words meant.

Unfortunately, when they got back to Grandma's house, they found out that she wasn't at home. The two friends didn't know what to do, so they decided to go back out and look for Grandma. 

Luckily, they eventually found her and they showed her the paper. Grandma was very surprised when she saw it, but she was able to tell them what the words meant. 

The two friends were so glad to have finally figured out the words, and that their decision to show Grandma had worked out in the end!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to act and play with her toys in the garage. The garage was her favorite place because it was big and fun.

One day, Lucy found a gentle cat in the garage. The cat was soft and nice. Lucy and the cat played together all day. They acted like they were in a big show for everyone to see.

In the end, Lucy and the gentle cat were very happy. They played in the garage every day and acted in many fun shows. They were the best of friends and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Daisy and Sam. Daisy and Sam loved to dance together. They would dance in the park and together in the garden.

One day a war broke out. Daisy was very afraid. She felt worried about what was going to happen.

But then Sam said he had a plan. He told Daisy that if they danced together, no bad things could happen to them. So Daisy and Sam started to dance. 

They danced and danced and soon the war stopped. Daisy was no longer scared.

Daisy and Sam were very happy and they kept dancing together. Whenever something bad happened they danced, and they were never scared again.

Sara and Tom moved to a new house with Mom and Dad. They had many boxes to unpack. Sara wanted to unpack her toys and books. Tom wanted to unpack his cars and trains. Mom and Dad wanted to unpack the dishes and clothes.

But the new house was very gloomy. It had no curtains, no lamps, no pictures. It was dark and cold. And it had a lot of dust. Sara sneezed when she opened a box. Tom coughed when he moved a chair. Mom and Dad wiped their hands on their shirts.

"Mom, I don't like this house," Sara said. "It makes me sad."

"Me too," Tom said. "It makes me sick."

Mom and Dad hugged them. "Don't worry, my loves," Mom said. "We will make this house bright and warm. We will hang curtains, lamps, and pictures. We will clean the dust and make it shine. We will fill it with our things and our love. Then it will be our home."

Sara and Tom smiled. They helped Mom and Dad unpack the boxes. They found their toys and books, their cars and trains. They put them in their rooms. They made their beds. They played together.

The new house was not so gloomy anymore. It had some color, some light, some life. It had Sara and Tom, Mom and Dad. It had their home.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toy guns and pretend to shoot bad guys. One day, Timmy and his friends went to play at the park. They saw a big, flexible tree that they wanted to climb, but it was too high.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was coming from the church across the street. Timmy and his friends ran to see what was happening. They saw a man with a gun trying to rob the church! Timmy knew what to do. He took out his toy gun and pretended to shoot the bad guy.

The robber got scared and ran away. Timmy and his friends were heroes! They climbed the flexible tree and celebrated their victory. From that day on, Timmy knew that he could use his toy gun to protect others and be a good guy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat corn. One day, she went to the farm to pick some corn. It was difficult for her to pick the corn because it was too tall for her. 

She asked the farmer, "Can you help me pick the corn? It's difficult for me." 

The farmer said, "Sure, I understand. Let me help you." 

Together, they picked the corn and Lily was very happy. She said, "Thank you for helping me. I love corn!" 

The farmer smiled and said, "I'm glad I could help. Corn is delicious!" 

From that day on, Lily always went to the farm to pick corn with the farmer. She understood that it was easier to pick corn with a friend.

Once upon a time, there lived a bear. His favourite thing to do was write. He loved to write stories, letters and even poems. He wrote every day.

One day, he heard a mysterious sound coming from the woods. He followed the sound, and soon he saw a bell. The bell was hanging from a tree and it rang each time the wind blew.

The bear was curious so he took the bell home. He wrote stories about the bell and its mysterious sound. Everyone loved the stories and soon everywhere people began ringing their own bells.

The bear was delighted. He had used his writing to share something very special in the world. He kept the mysterious bell close by, for it was his favourite story reminder.

Once there was a great girl named Jane. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day she saw a big pile of cardboard in the yard. Jane asked her mom: "What is this?"

Her mom said, "That is cardboard, Jane. You can make anything with it!"

Jane was so excited she couldn't wait to see what she could make. She grabbed some pieces and started to build. She built a great castle with walls and towers. She asked her mom if she could color it.

Her mom said yes and gave Jane some markers to use. Jane colored the castle and it looked even better. She was so proud of her great creation and she couldn't wait to show it to her friends. The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved to explore the world around her. One day, she went for a walk in the forest and saw a big, brown bear.

"Hello, Mr. Bear! How are you?" asked Lily.

"I'm doing well, thank you," replied the bear.

Lily was surprised that the bear could talk. She looked at him with wide eyes and nodded her head.

The bear noticed Lily's curious expression and said, "Would you like to touch my ear?"

Lily nodded again and gently touched the bear's furry ear. It was soft and warm.

From that day on, Lily and the bear became good friends and went on many adventures together in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw a pretty butterfly and chased it all around the garden. When the butterfly landed on a flower, Lily gently covered it with her hand to keep it safe.

Later that day, Lily's mom told her about a war that happened a long time ago. Lily didn't understand what war meant, but she could tell it made her mom sad. She gave her mom a big hug to make her feel better.

In the evening, Lily's dad read her a charming story before bedtime. It was about a princess who lived in a castle and went on adventures with her friends. Lily loved the story and fell asleep dreaming of castles and princesses.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient tree in the forest. The tree was very tall and had many branches. One day, a child came to play near the tree. The child saw a big stick and picked it up. The child started hitting the tree with the stick. Suddenly, one of the branches snapped and fell to the ground. 

The tree was very angry and said to the child, "Why did you snap my branch? That hurt me!" The child was scared and said, "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to hurt you. I was just playing." The tree replied, "It's okay, but please be careful. I am very old and fragile." The child promised to be more careful and they became friends. From that day on, the child played near the tree but never hit it again.

name_of_work: What Are Years by Marianne Moore
content: What is our innocence, what is our guilt? All are naked, none is safe. And whence is courage: the unanswered question, the resolute doubt-- dumbly calling, deafly listening--that in misfortune, even death, encourages others and in its defeat, stirs the soul to be strong? He sees deep and is glad, who accedes to mortality and in his imprisonment, rises upon himself as the sea in a chasm, struggling to be free and unable to be, in its surrendering finds its continuing. So he who strongly feels, behaves. The very bird, grown taller as he sings, steels his form straight up. Though he is captive, his mighty singing says, satisfaction is a lowly thing, how pure a thing is joy. This is mortality, this is eternity.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Sam. Sam had a bottle that he liked very much. One day, his sister started to tease Sam about his bottle. She said it was too noisy when he played with it. Sam was sad and he didn't know what to do.

Then, Sam's mom came over and saw what was happening. She gave Sam and his sister a big hug and said, "Practice being kind to each other. It's more fun to help each other than to tease." Sam and his sister agreed with Mom.

From then on, Sam's bottle stayed very happy in his hands. He would play with it very carefully and his sister would help him when it got too noisy. Sam and his sister had lots of fun together. The end.

name_of_work: No Men Are Foreign by James Kirkup
content: Have you ever thought of some people as strange or other countries as foreign? We have many ways of thinking of other people as different from us as them. They may belong to a different country, or speak a different language. In this poem, however, the poet reminds us of the many ways in which we are all the same -- for we are all human. Remember, no men are strange, no countries foreign Beneath all uniforms, a single body breathes Like ours: the land our brothers walk upon Is earth like this, in which we all shall lie. They, too, aware of sun and air and water, Are fed by peaceful harvests, by war's long winter starv'd. Their hands are ours, and in their lines we read A labour not different from our own. Remember they have eyes like ours that wake Or sleep, and strength that can be won By love. In every land is common life That all can recognise and understand. Let us remember, whenever we are told To hate our brothers, it is ourselves That we shall dispossess, betray, condemn. Remember, we who take arms against each other It is the human earth that we defile. Our hells of fire and dust outrage the innocence Of air that is everywhere our own, Remember, no men are foreign, and no countries strange.

name_of_work: As Kingfishers Catch Fire by Gerard Manley Hopkins
content: As kingfishers catch fire, dragonflies draw flame; As tumbled over rim in roundy wells Stones ring; like each tucked string tells, each hung bell's Bow swung finds tongue to fling out broad its name; Each mortal thing does one thing and the same: Deals out that being indoors each one dwells; Selves -- goes itself; myself it speaks and spells, Crying What I do is me: for that I came. I say more: the just man justices; Keeps grace: that keeps all his goings graces; Acts in God's eye what in God's eye he is -- Christ -- for Christ plays in ten thousand places, Lovely in limbs, and lovely in eyes not his To the Father through the features of men's faces.

Once, there was a little girl named Sally. She loved to wear her red shoes wherever she would go. One day, she decided to go to the park and wear them there. 

When she arrived, she found a mixer in the playground. She was so curious, she decided to touch it.

"Oh no," Sally cried, because she accidentally made it wet. 

"You shouldn't have touched that," her friend said. "Now we'll get in trouble."

But it was too late. A grown-up saw them and they were both sent home. 

From that day on, Sally promised never to touch a mixer again. And she never did. The end.

Tom and Anna like to play hide and seek. They have a big maze in their garden. The maze has many paths and walls made of green plants. It is fun to run and hide in the maze.

One day, Tom and Anna play hide and seek with their friend Ben. Ben is good at finding them. He knows the maze very well. He can see their feet under the plants. He can hear their giggles behind the walls.

Tom and Anna want to trick Ben. They have a plan. They find a secret door in the maze. The door leads to a different maze. This maze is not regular. It has many colors and shapes and sounds. It is like a magic maze.

Tom and Anna go through the door and hide in the magic maze. They wait for Ben to find them. But Ben does not come. He looks for them in the regular maze. He does not see the door. He does not hear their voices. He is confused and sad.

Tom and Anna hear Ben calling their names. They feel sorry for him. They go back to the regular maze. They find Ben and hug him. They tell him about the secret door and the magic maze. They invite him to play with them there. Ben is happy and curious. They all go through the door and have fun in the magic maze.

Ben and Lily are playing in the park. They see a big dog with a long tail. The dog is friendly and wags its tail. Ben and Lily want to pet the dog, but they are not sure if they can.

They see a man walking with the dog. The man has a leash around his waist. He sees Ben and Lily and smiles.

"Hello, do you like my dog?" he asks. "His name is Max. He is very nice and gentle. Do you want to say hello to him?"

Ben and Lily nod. They are curious and excited. The man kneels down and shows them how to pet Max. He tells them to be gentle and not to pull his ears or tail.

"Good, you are very good with dogs," he says. "Max likes you. You can give him a treat if you want. I have some in my pocket."

He takes out a small biscuit and gives it to Ben. Ben holds it in his hand and offers it to Max. Max sniffs it and licks it. Then he takes it gently and chews it. He wags his tail again.

"Wow, he likes it!" Ben says. "Can I give him another one?"

"Sure, but only one more," the man says. "He has to watch his waist. He is a big dog, but he can get fat if he eats too much."

He gives another biscuit to Lily. Lily does the same as Ben. Max eats it and licks her hand. He looks happy.

"Thank you for the treats," the man says. "You are very kind and polite. Max and I have to go now. We have a serious appointment at the vet. He needs a check-up and a shot. He doesn't like it, but it's good for him."

"Bye, Max. Bye, man," Ben and Lily say. "We hope you are well and not sick."

They wave as the man and the dog walk away. They go back to playing in the park. They like Max. He is a nice dog. They hope to see him again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside in his backyard. One day, he found a big stick and pretended it was a sword. He swung the stick around and made whooshing sounds. Suddenly, he accidentally struck his dad's flower pot and it shattered into a million pieces.

Timmy felt really bad, but his dad told him it was okay and they would clean it up together. After they finished, Timmy went to play in his little hut. It was made of cardboard boxes and was his favorite place to hide. He pretended he was a knight defending his castle from dragons.

As he played, he noticed a strange smell. He looked around and saw that his sister had put a fake spider in his hut. Timmy laughed and said "that's silly!" and continued playing.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. She was three years old and loved to cook. One day, she wanted to make something special, so she grabbed a bowl and some ingredients. Then she decided to make a cross shaped cake. 

She combined the ingredients and baked the cake in the oven. As soon as it was out of the oven, Mia was so excited to look at her finished creation. But when she looked the cake was scary! It was big and black!
