Lily and Ben are playing in the living room. They have many toys and books, but they both want the same thing: the black cushion. The black cushion is soft and big, and they like to hug it and jump on it.

"Give me the black cushion!" Lily says. She tries to pull it from Ben's arms.

"No, it's mine!" Ben says. He holds it tight and pushes Lily away.

They start to fight and shout. They pull and tug and kick. The black cushion is in the middle of their fight.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees Lily and Ben fighting over the black cushion. She is not happy.

"Stop it, both of you!" Mom says. "Why are you fighting over the black cushion?"

"Because it's mine!" Lily and Ben say at the same time.

Mom shakes her head. She picks up the black cushion and puts it on the sofa.

"Listen, Lily and Ben," Mom says. "The black cushion is not yours or mine. It is for everyone to share. If you both want it, you have to ask nicely and take turns. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nod. They feel sorry for fighting.

"Can I have the black cushion first, please?" Lily asks.

"OK, you can have it first," Ben says. "But only for five minutes. Then it's my turn."

"Thank you, Ben," Lily says. She smiles and hugs the black cushion.

"You're welcome, Lily," Ben says. He smiles and picks up a book.

Mom smiles too. She is glad that Lily and Ben are playing nicely again. She sits on the sofa and watches them. She hopes they will share the black cushion and other things too.

LIKE a skein of loose silk blown against a wall She walks by the railing of a path in Kensington Gardens, And she is dying piece-meal of a sort of emotional anemia. And round about there is a rabble Of the filthy, sturdy, unkillable infants of the very poor. They shall inherit the earth. In her is the end of breeding. Her boredom is exquisite and excessive. She would like some one to speak to her, And is almost afraid that I will commit that indiscretion.

Nights like this: on the cold apple bough a white star, then another exploding out of the bark: on the ground, moonlight picking at small stones as it picks greater stones, as it rises with the surf laying its cheek for moments on the sand as it licks the broken ledge, as it flows up the cliffs, as it flicks across the tracks as it unavailing pours into the gash of the sand-and-gravel quarry as it leans across the hangared fuselage of the crop-dusting plane as it soaks through cracks into trailers tremulous with sleep as it dwells upon the eyelids of the sleepers as if to make amends.

name_of_work: Winter Landscape, with Rooks by Sylvia Plath
content: Water in the millrace, through a sluice of stone, plunges headlong into that black pond where, absurd and out-of-season, a single swan floats chaste as snow, taunting the clouded mind which hungers to haul the white reflection down. The austere sun descends above the fen, an orange cyclops-eye, scorning to look longer on this landscape of chagrin; feathered dark in thought, I stalk like a rook, brooding as the winter night comes on. Last summer's reeds are all engraved in ice as is your image in my eye; dry frost glazes the window of my hurt; what solace can be struck from rock to make heart's waste grow green again? Who'd walk in this bleak place?

Often I had gone this way before: But now it seemed I never could be And never had been anywhere else; 'Twas home; one nationality We had, I and the birds that sang, One memory. They welcomed me. I had come back That eve somehow from somewhere far: The April mist, the chill, the calm, Meant the same thing familiar And pleasant to us, and strange too, Yet with no bar. The thrush on the oaktop in the lane Sang his last song, or last but one; And as he ended, on the elm Another had but just begun His last; they knew no more than I The day was done. Then past his dark white cottage front A labourer went along, his tread Slow, half with weariness, half with ease; And, through the silence, from his shed The sound of sawing rounded all That silence said.

"How often the lone-dweller anticipates some sign, this Measurer's mercy -- must always must-- mind-caring, along the ocean's windings, stirring rime-chill seas, hands as oars many long whiles, treading the tracks of exile-- the way of the world an open book always." (1-5) So spoke the earth-stepper, a memorial of miseries slaughter of the wrathful, crumbling of kinsmen: "Often, every daybreak, alone I must bewail my cares. There's now no one living to whom I dare mumble my mind's understanding. I know as truth that it's seen suitable for anyone to bind fast their spirit's closet, hold onto the hoards, think whatever -- (8-14) "Can a weary mind weather the shitstorm? I think not. Can a roiling heart set itself free? I don't think so. So often those hustling for the win must clamp down grim mindings in their coffer, just as I ought fetter my inborn conceit, often wounded, wanting where I know, kindred pulled away, how many winters now? I shrouded my giver in dark earth and wended away worrisome, weather-watching the wrapful waves, hall-wretched, seeking a center, far or near, where they might be found, in some mead-hall, who knows of my kind, willing to adopt a friendless me, though they be joyful enough. (15-29a) "The well-travelled know how slicing sorrow can be by one's side, short a struggle-friend, however dear. The ways of wandering wind him round not even a wire of wound gold-- a frigid fastness, hardly any fruits of the fold. This one lists the hall-lads swilling rings, giver-drenched in youngsome days, in both furnishing and feasting. Joys all flown, vanished all away! (29b-36) "Therefore one knows who long forgoes the friendly words of their first, when sleep and sorrow stand together clutching at the crestfallen alone. Somehow seems that somewhere inside this one enwraps his lord and kisses his lord, and laps both hands and head on his knee, when, once upon a year blurry in time now, one thrived by the throne -- too soon rousing, a friendless singular seeing all around a fallowness of waves, sea-birds bathing, fanning their feathers, ice and snow hurtling, heaved up with hail. (37-48) "So heavy and heavier the hurt in heart harrowing for the lost. Sorrow made new whenever recalling pervades the mind, greeting kindred joyfully, drinking in the look of them fellowable and fathoming-- they always swim away. Gulls ghost-call -- I don't know their tongue too well, much of their comfort weird. Worrying made new to that one who must send more and more, every day, a bleary soul back across the binding of waves. (49-57) "Therefore I cannot wonder across this world why my mind does not muster in the murk when I ponder pervading all the lives of humans, how suddenly they abandon their halls, proud princes and young. Right here in the middle it fumbles and falls every day -- (58-63) "No one can be wise before earning their lot of winters in this world. The wise one, they stay patient: not too heart-heated, not so hasty to harp, not too weak-armed, nor too wan-headed, nor too fearful nor too fey nor too fee-felching, and never tripping the tongue too much, before it trips them. (64-9) "That one bides their moment to make brag, until the inner fire seizes its moment clearly, to where their secret self veers them. Who's wise must fore-ken how ghostly it has been when the world and its things stand wasted -- like you find, here and there, in this middle space now -- there walls totter, wailed around by winds, gnashed by frost, the buildings snow-lapt. The winehalls molder, their wielder lies washed clean of joys, his peerage all perished, proud by the wall. War ravaged a bunch ferried along the forth-way, others a raptor ravished over lofty seas, this one the hoary wolf broke in its banes, the last a brother graveled in the ground, tears as war-mask. (70-84) "That's the way it goes-- the Shaper mills middle-earth to waste until they stand empty, the giants' work and ancient, drained of the dreams and joys of its dwellers." (85-7) Then one wisely regards this wall-stead, deliberates a darkened existence, aged in spirit, often remembering from afar many war-slaughterings, and speaks these words: (88-91) "Where has the horse gone? Where are my kindred? Where is the giver of treasure? Where are the benches to bear us? Joys of the hall to bring us together? No more, the bright goblet! All gone, the mailed warrior! Lost for good, the pride of princes! "How the space of years has spread -- growing gloomy beneath the night-helm, as if it never was! (92-6) "Tracks of the beloved multitude, all that remains walls wondrous tall, serpents seething-- thanes stolen, pillaged by ashen foes gear glutting for slaughter -- we know this world's way, and the storms still batter these stony cliffs. The tumbling snows stumble up the earth, the clash of winter, when darkness descends. Night-shadows benighten, sent down from the north, raw showers of ice, who doesn't hate humanity? (97-105) All shot through in misery in earthly realms, fortune's turn turns the world under sky. Here the cash was a loan. Your friends were a loan. Anyone at all, a loan. Your family only ever a loan-- And this whole foundation of the earth wastes away!" (106-10) So says the wise one, you don't hear him at all, sitting apart reading their own runes. (111) It's better to clutch at your counsel, you ought never manifest your miseries not too quickly where they well, unless the balm is clear beforehand, keep whittling at your courage. (112-14a) It will be well for those who seek the favor, the comfort from our father in heaven, where a battlement bulwarks us all. (114b-5)

name_of_work: To BRYANT, the Poet of Nature by Walt Whitman
content: Let Glory diadem the mighty dead-- Let monuments of brass and marble rise To those who have upon our being shed A golden halo, borrowed from the skies, And given to time its most enduring prize; For they but little less than angels were: But not to thee, oh! nature's OWN, we should (When from this clod the minstrel-soul aspires And joins the glorious band of purer lyres) Tall columns build: thy monument is here-- For ever fixed in its eternity-- A monument God-built! 'Tis seen around-- In mountains huge and many gliding streams-- Where'er the torrent lifts a melancholy sound, Or modest flower in broad savannah gleams.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Rose. She was cheerful and always eager to explore. One day, she decided to take a walk around her garden. 

She found a beautiful flower and decided to stay and admire it. But as soon as she approached the flower, she started to sneeze! She sneezed so much that she had to close her eyes and cover her nose. After a few moments, she opened her eyes again. 

Suddenly, she heard a voice. It said, "Thank you for sneezing, Rose!" She turned around and saw a fairy with bright pink eyes. The fairy smiled and said," I needed a good sneeze to help me spread my sparkly dust!" 

Rose was so excited to meet the fairy that she was eager to help her. She sneezed as many times as she could, and the fairy covered the whole garden in its sparkly dust. 

When the fairy was done, she thanked Rose and flew away. Rose was thrilled and happily stayed in the garden, gazing at the beautiful sparkles all around her.

name_of_work: A Dog Has Died by Pablo Neruda
content: My dog has died. I buried him in the garden next to a rusted old machine. Some day I'll join him right there, but now he's gone with his shaggy coat, his bad manners and his cold nose, and I, the materialist, who never believed in any promised heaven in the sky for any human being, I believe in a heaven I'll never enter. Yes, I believe in a heaven for all dogdom where my dog waits for my arrival waving his fan-like tail in friendship. Ai, I'll not speak of sadness here on earth, of having lost a companion who was never servile. His friendship for me, like that of a porcupine withholding its authority, was the friendship of a star, aloof, with no more intimacy than was called for, with no exaggerations: he never climbed all over my clothes filling me full of his hair or his mange, he never rubbed up against my knee like other dogs obsessed with sex. No, my dog used to gaze at me, paying me the attention I need, the attention required to make a vain person like me understand that, being a dog, he was wasting time, but, with those eyes so much purer than mine, he'd keep on gazing at me with a look that reserved for me alone all his sweet and shaggy life, always near me, never troubling me, and asking nothing. Ai, how many times have I envied his tail as we walked together on the shores of the sea in the lonely winter of Isla Negra where the wintering birds filled the sky and my hairy dog was jumping about full of the voltage of the sea's movement: my wandering dog, sniffing away with his golden tail held high, face to face with the ocean's spray. Joyful, joyful, joyful, as only dogs know how to be happy with only the autonomy of their shameless spirit. There are no good-byes for my dog who has died, and we don't now and never did lie to each other. So now he's gone and I buried him, and that's all there is to it.

Once upon a time there was a sleepy little bear called Ted. He was so tired that he couldn't keep his eyes open any longer. So, Ted curled up in a big warm bed and went to sleep. 

In the morning, Ted woke up with a big surprise. He saw a big smile on his mum's face! Ted smiled back, forgetting all about how tired he had been the night before.

His Mum had a surprise for him - a big, soft toy! Ted was so excited that he couldn't help but smile. He cuddled the toy and promised to take care of it forever.

But then Ted was sleepy again, and so he went back to bed and tucked himself up in the covers. And with the new toy by his side, the sleepy bear was soon fast asleep again.

Once upon a time, there was a fox. The good fox wanted to increase something, but he didn't know what. He looked around, but he couldn't figure it out. Then, he spotted a bird perched in a tree. The fox asked the bird, "Can you tell me something to increase?" The bird thought for a moment, then said, "You can increase your happiness!" The fox was delighted. He thanked the bird and set off to find happiness.

He looked everywhere but couldn't find it. He looked in the trees, under rocks, and even in a lake. He still couldn't find it. Then, he decided to take a nap and maybe he would find it upon waking up. As he slowly drifted off to sleep, he dreamed of happiness. When he woke up, he felt full of joy and he knew he had found it!

name_of_work: To My Daughter On Being Separated from Her on Her Marriage by Anne Hunter
content: Dear to my heart as life's warm stream Which animates this mortal clay, For thee I court the waking dream, And deck with smiles the future day; And thus beguile the present pain With hopes that we shall meet again. Yet, will it be as when the past Twined every joy, and care, and thought, And o'er our minds one mantle cast Of kind affections finely wrought? Ah no! the groundless hope were vain, For so we ne'er can meet again! May he who claims thy tender heart Deserve its love, as I have done! For, kind and gentle as thou art, If so beloved, thou art fairly won. Bright may the sacred torch remain, And cheer thee till we meet again!

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there was a playful dog named Spot. Spot loved to jump and play all day. He was always happy and full of energy.

One sunny day, Spot's owner, a little girl named Sue, had a task for him. She wanted Spot to help her find her lost ball. Sue said, "Spot, let's find my ball. Can you help me?" Spot wagged his tail and barked, "Yes, I can help!"

Sue and Spot started to look for the ball. They looked under the trees and behind the bushes. Spot jumped high and low to find the ball. Finally, Spot found the ball in a big pile of leaves. He jumped and grabbed the ball with his mouth.

Sue clapped her hands and said, "Good job, Spot! You found my ball!" Spot was so happy and proud. They both laughed and continued to play together in the park. And from that day on, Spot and Sue were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack who loved to play with wool. Every day, he woke up early in the morning and went to the garden outside to collect some wool from the sheep. 

One day, when Jack was playing in the garden, he saw a silly rabbit hopping from bush to bush. Jack thought it was very funny and he started to giggle. 

The rabbit then said, "Stop laughing! Don't be so stupid!" Jack replied, "I'm not being stupid, I'm just having fun!" 

The rabbit then said, "Let's make a deal. If you shake this wool, it will grow longer and I can use it to make a nice warm home. What do you say?" 

Jack thought it was a great idea, so he picked up the wool and started to shake it vigorously. After a while, the wool got longer and longer and the rabbit was so happy! It was a perfect home to live in. 

Jack had a lot of fun that day and he also learned a valuable lesson. He learned that being silly can sometimes lead to great things.

Lily loves to sing. She sings all the time. She sings in the morning, in the afternoon, and at night. She sings to her toys, to her mom, and to her dad. She sings loud and happy.

One day, Lily sees a microphone in the store. It is shiny and big. It has a button and a cord. Lily wants the microphone. She asks her mom, "Can I have the microphone, please?"

Her mom says, "Why do you want the microphone, Lily?"

Lily says, "Because I love to sing. And the microphone makes my voice louder and better. And I can sing to more people. And they will like my songs. And I will be important."

Her mom smiles and hugs Lily. She says, "Lily, you are important. You are important to me, and to dad, and to your toys. And you have a beautiful voice. You don't need a microphone to sing. You can sing with your heart. And I will always listen to you."

Lily thinks for a moment. She says, "You are right, mom. I don't need a microphone. I have you. And you are the best listener. Can we sing together?"

Her mom says, "Of course, Lily. Let's sing together. What song do you want to sing?"

Lily says, "I want to sing the song you taught me. The one that says, 'I love you, you love me, we are a happy family.'"

Her mom says, "I know that song. I love that song. Let's sing it loud and happy."

And they sing the song, holding hands, in the store. And they don't care about the microphone. And they are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big musician who loved to play music. He had a large guitar that he played every day. One day, he went to a party and ate too much cake. The cake made him feel sick and his stomach hurt. He had spoiled his appetite. 

The musician tried to play his guitar, but he felt too sick. He had to go home and rest. He felt sad because he wanted to play music all night long. But he knew he had to take care of himself first. 

The next day, he felt better and played his guitar again. He played beautiful music and everyone loved it. He realized that taking care of himself was important so he wouldn't spoil his fun. From that day on, he made sure to eat healthy and take breaks so he could keep playing music for a long, long time.

name_of_work: In Wales, wanting to be Italian by Imtiaz Dharker
content: Is there a name for that thing you do when you are young? There must be a word for it in some language, probably German, or if not just asking to be made up, something like Fremdlandischgehorenlust or perhaps Einzumandererslandgehorenwunsch. What is it called, living in Glasgow, dying to be French, dying to shrug and pout and make yourself understood without saying a word? Have you ever felt like that, being in Bombay, wanting to declare, like Freddy Mercury, that you are from somewhere like Zanzibar? What is it called? Being sixteen in Wales, longing to be Italian, to be able to say aloud, without embarrassment, Bella! Bella! lounge by a Vespa with a cigarette hanging out of your mouth, and wear impossibly pointed shoes?

The hounds, you know them all by name. You fostered them from purblind whelps At their dam's teats, and you have come To know the music of their yelps: High-strung Anthee, the brindled bitch, The blue-tick coated Philomel, And freckled Chloe, who would fetch A pretty price if you would sell-- All fleet of foot, and swift to scent, Inexorable once on the track, Like angry words you might have meant, But do not mean, and can't take back. There was a time when you would brag How they would bay and rend apart The hopeless belling from a stag. You falter now for the foundered hart. Desires you nursed of a winter night-- Did you know then why you bred them-- Whose needling milk-teeth used to bite The master's hand that leashed and fed them?

name_of_work: Suicide in the Trenches by Siegfried Sassoon
content: I knew a simple soldier boy Who grinned at life in empty joy, Slept soundly through the lonesome dark, And whistled early with the lark. In winter trenches, cowed and glum, With crumps and lice and lack of rum, He put a bullet through his brain. No one spoke of him again. You smug-faced crowds with kindling eye Who cheer when soldier lads march by, Sneak home and pray you'll never know The hell where youth and laughter go.

I must not think of thee; and, tired yet strong, I shun the thought that lurks in all delight-- The thought of thee--and in the blue heaven's height, And in the sweetest passage of a song. Oh, just beyond the fairest thoughts that throng This breast, the thought of thee waits hidden yet bright; But it must never, never come in sight; I must stop short of thee the whole day long. But when sleep comes to close each difficult day, When night gives pause to the long watch I keep, And all my bonds I needs must loose apart, Must doff my will as raiment laid away,-- With the first dream that comes with the first sleep I run, I run, I am gathered to thy heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit. The rabbit had a broken leg. It hurt a lot. The rabbit was sad.

One day, the rabbit saw a big tree. The tree had a small hole. The rabbit went close to the hole. The rabbit went inside the hole. The hole was warm and safe.

The rabbit lived in the hole for many days. The rabbit's broken leg got better. The rabbit was happy. The rabbit played with friends. The rabbit and friends lived close to the tree. They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a kind and compassionate bunny. Every day the bunny liked to jog in the park. One day while the bunny was jogging, he heard a stirring in a nearby bush. He stopped to investigate and found a little baby bird who had fallen out of her nest.

The bunny was so compassionate that he wanted to help the baby bird get back in her nest. He examined the branch, and found a way to place the bird back safely. He gently stirred the bush until the bird was able to jump into the nest.

The bunny was so proud that he was able to help the little bird get back home. He watched her chirping sweetly to her mommy. He said goodbye and went back to jogging, but he felt very happy inside.

Lily is a bird who loves to fly. She has two healthy wings that help her soar in the sky. She likes to sing and play with her friends in the trees. She is happy and free.

One day, she meets a boy who is sad. He is sitting on a bench and holding a toy plane. He says, "I wish I could fly like you. I want to see the clouds and the sun. But I have no wings. I only have this plane, and it is broken."

Lily feels sorry for the boy. She says, "You can fly with me. I can share my wings with you. I will hold you and take you up in the air. You can see the clouds and the sun. You can be happy and free."

The boy smiles and says, "Really? You would do that for me? You are very kind. But how can you share your wings with me? You need them to fly. You own them. They are yours."

Lily says, "I own my wings, but I can also share them. Sharing is good. It makes me and you happy. Come, hold my feet and I will lift you up. You will see how fun it is to fly."

The boy holds Lily's feet and she flaps her wings. They rise up in the air and fly together. They see the clouds and the sun. They feel the wind and the joy. They sing and play in the sky. They are happy and free.

Lily liked to record her voice with her toy phone. She would say funny things and then listen to them. She thought it was fun to hear herself talk.

One day, she found a gray phone in her mom's room. It looked like her toy phone, but bigger and heavier. Lily wanted to try it. She picked it up and pressed the red button.

"Hello, hello, this is Lily. I am a big girl. I can record my voice with this phone. Do you like my voice?" she said into the phone.

She pressed the red button again and waited for her voice to come back. But nothing happened. She pressed the button again and again, but still nothing.

She felt sad and angry. Why did the gray phone not work like her toy phone? She threw the phone on the bed and started to cry.

Mom heard the noise and came into the room. She saw Lily crying and the gray phone on the bed. She knew what happened.

"Oh, Lily, I'm sorry. This is not a regular phone. This is a special phone that I use for work. It does not record your voice. It only sends messages to other people. You can't play with it. It's not a toy." she said.

She picked up the phone and checked if it was still working. She saw that Lily had sent a message to her boss. She felt embarrassed and worried.

She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, honey. You didn't know. But you have to ask me before you touch my things. And you have to be careful with them. They are not for fun. They are for important things."

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I won't touch your phone again. Can I play with my toy phone?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can. But first, let me call my boss and explain what happened. Maybe he will think your voice is funny too."

Once there was a group of friends who were playing in the park. They were very happy and enjoyed exploring the park together. 
After a while, one of the friends had an idea. She pulled out a shiny spoon from her pocket and said, "Let's play with this spoon!" Everyone loved the idea and they took the spoon to the deepest part of the park. 

Once they arrived at a deep pond, they decided to introduce the spoon to the water. The spoon glided gracefully through the water, quickly becoming everyone's favorite toy.

The friends had a wonderful time playing with the spoon in the pond. They laughed and waved the spoon through the water, making big ripples and watching the sun sparkle on the surface. It was a magical day!

Oh mother, mother, where is happiness? They took my lover's tallness off to war, Left me lamenting. Now I cannot guess What I can use an empty heart-cup for. He won't be coming back here any more. Some day the war will end, but, oh, I knew When he went walking grandly out that door That my sweet love would have to be untrue. Would have to be untrue. Would have to court Coquettish death, whose impudent and strange Possessive arms and beauty (of a sort) Can make a hard man hesitate--and change. And he will be the one to stammer, "Yes." Oh mother, mother, where is happiness?

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Isla. She loved listening to stories about far-away islands and dreaming about what it would be like to watch the sea from the top of a mountain. 

One day, Isla heard a strange noise coming from her living room. She went to investigate and found a large box that was shaking. Cautiously, she opened it and out sprang an island with palm trees swaying in the breeze! Isla couldn't believe her eyes. 

The island asked Isla if she wanted to climb the highest peak and see the world from here. Without hesitating, Isla said yes. She knew her mom didn't want her to wander too far, so she carefully climbed the mountain, while making sure not to go too fast. 

At the peak, Isla was blown away by the beautiful sight of the sea.  She noticed a shadow in the distance, that looked a lot like her mom. Suddenly Isla realised she had gone too far and became ashamed that she had disobeyed. 

When Isla reached her mom, all she could do was look down and listen as her mom lectured her for not listening to the rules. She knew she would never forget this lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who loved to sing. Every day, she would fly around the forest and sing beautiful songs. All the animals loved to listen to her sweet sound.

One day, a big, mean cat came into the forest. He didn't like the little bird's singing and thought it was disgusting. He wanted the bird to stop singing so he could sleep in peace.

The little bird didn't want to stop singing, but she was afraid of the cat. She asked her animal friends for help. They all came together and made loud sounds to scare the cat away. The cat ran away and the little bird could sing happily again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, she was playing and hiding behind a big curtain. Suddenly, she heard her friend calling her name. "Lily, come out! We found you!" 

Lily tried to move but the curtain was stuck. She felt uncomfortable and scared. She called out to her friends, "Help me, I'm stuck behind the curtain!" Her friends rushed over and pulled the curtain, freeing Lily. 

After the game, Lily's friends told her that it's important to always speak up when you're uncomfortable or in trouble. They reminded her that they were there to help her, and that friends always come to each other's aid. Lily learned an important lesson that day, and from then on, she always spoke up when she needed help.

Ben and Lily were on the same team for the art project. They had to wash their hands before they could use the paints. But Ben did not want to wash his hands. He said he was not dirty.

"Ben, you have to wash your hands," Lily said. "The teacher said so. And the paints are messy. You will make our team look bad."

"No, I don't," Ben said. "I like my hands like this. They have cool colors from the crayons. And I don't care what the teacher says. She is harsh. She always tells us what to do."

Lily was angry. She did not like Ben's attitude. She thought he was rude and selfish. She wanted to do a good job on the art project. She wanted their team to be proud.

"Ben, you are being silly," Lily said. "Washing your hands is easy and fun. Look, there is a soap that smells like strawberries. And there is a towel that is soft and fluffy. Come on, let's wash our hands together."

Ben looked at the soap and the towel. He smelled the strawberries. He felt the softness. He thought maybe washing his hands was not so bad. He saw Lily smiling at him. He thought maybe she was not so harsh. He thought maybe he could be nice to her.

"Okay, Lily," Ben said. "Let's wash our hands. And then let's do a great art project. We are a good team, right?"

Lily nodded. She was happy. She took Ben's hand and led him to the sink. They washed their hands and dried them. They went back to their table and picked up their paints. They worked together and made a beautiful picture. They were a good team.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very obedient, and never did anything that her mom and dad said she shouldn't do.

One day, as she was walking with her mom and dad, a stranger came up to them. The little girl was scared of him, and tried to stay close to her parents.

The stranger smiled at the little girl and started to poke her with a finger. She was very frightened and moved away from him.

Her parents stepped in and told the stranger to leave. He looked sad, but he obeyed them, and soon he was gone. 

The family returned home safely, and the little girl felt so relieved. From then on, she was extra obedient and never strayed too far away from her parents.

John and his mom went to the park. John was very excited because he got to play with his wagon! He loaded it up with rocks, twigs, and flowers. 

John and his mom walked around the park. He waved at the other kids and said hello to all the dogs. But then he saw something very unusual. There was a grumpy old man sitting on the bench. 

John was scared of the man. He hid behind his mom and held on to his wagon. The grumpy old man started to laugh and waved at John. John was surprised and slowly walked over to say hello. 

The old man smiled and showed John his wagon. He helped John load it up with even more interesting things like pine cones and feathers. John and the old man played together and soon they were both happy and laughing. 

John dragged his heavy wagon home. He had a great time at the park and couldn't wait to go back!

Once upon a time there was an amazing avocado tree. Every day the tree would give a special kind of fruit. The fruit was green and round, it was called an avocado.

One day, a little boy was walking by and noticed the avocado tree. He stopped to take a closer look. He said to himself, "That looks delicious!"

The little boy saw an old man sitting under the tree. He said, "Hello Mister! Can I have an avocado?"

The old man looked up and said, "I sure can give you an avocado, young man. But there's a catch. You must keep it safe and only eat it when the time is right."

The little boy was confused but he nodded and said, "Okay. I'll keep it safe."

He took the avocado and went home. He put it in a special drawer and waited.

A few days later, the little boy was hungry and decided to eat the avocado. He opened the drawer and was surprised! The avocado was larger and brighter than he had remembered. It tasted amazing!

The old man's words came back to the little boy, "Keep it safe and only eat it when the time is right". 
The little boy smiled, happy that he waited for the perfect time to enjoy the amazing avocado.

George was a sleepy bear. He yawned as he looked at the sky. He saw a triangle in the clouds. 

George felt a little troubled. He wanted to sleep but he was too awake. He looked around and saw a big tree. He went closer and saw a cozy spot underneath. 

He curled up and yawned again. Soon, George was fast asleep, dreaming about triangles in the clouds. 

When George woke up, he felt refreshed. He looked up and the triangle was still in the clouds. He smiled and waved at it, before walking off feeling much less troubled.

"Bye, Mommy!" Little Lily said with a smile as she zipped her purple coat and skipped down the front steps. 

Lily had big plans today. She was going to go to the park and trade with her friends. She knew she wanted to bring a tight hug - she could just feel it in her heart.

When she got to the park it was so much fun! Everyone was trading and playing games, but then something changed. Cassie said that she could only trade if Lily gave her one of her tight hugs.

Lily was so angry! She didn't understand why Cassie had to be so mean. She closed her eyes and wished for Cassie to be nicer.

Suddenly, Cassie didn't seem so mean anymore. "Let's just play", she said with a smile. Lily was so happy! She smiled wide and gave Cassie a tight hug. It was going to be a great day after all!

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Max. Max loved to play fetch and run in the park with his owner, Emily. One day, Emily decided to teach Max a new trick. She showed him how to sit and stay. Max was very cheerful and wagged his tail when he learned the trick.

After their training, Emily gave Max a treat. It was a bone that tasted very yummy. Max licked his lips and wagged his tail even more. He was very happy and grateful to his owner for teaching him something new. From then on, Max always sat and stayed when Emily asked him to, and he always got a tasty treat as a reward.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to a big building with her mom. They had to use the elevator to go up. Lily was excited because she loved the elevator. It went up and down, and made her tummy feel funny.

While they were waiting for the elevator, Lily saw a cute dog. She wanted to pet it. So, she wandered away from her mom to say hi to the dog. But the dog was angry and barked at Lily. This made her scared and she ran back to her mom.

Her mom hugged her and told her it was okay. They got on the elevator together and went up. Lily learned that it's not good to wander away from her mom, especially when there's an angry dog.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He was so happy he liked to skip everywhere he went. One day, Jack skipped to the bakery to buy a cake for him and his friends.

When Jack got there, he saw a beautiful cake. It was pink and covered in shiny sprinkles. Jack wanted to buy it right away.

The baker asked, "Do you have enough money to buy the cake?" 

Jack thought for a moment and said, "No, I don't have enough money to buy it. I'm sorry."

The baker smiled and said, "That's okay. You can have it for free! I'm happy to give it to you if it means you and your friends can be happy together." 

Jack was so happy he skipped all the way home with a big smile on his face. His friends were very happy when they saw the cake too. 

Moral of the story: It's important to be kind and generous to others, and when you do, it can make everyone happy.

I came from the sunny valleys And sought for the open sea, For I thought in its gray expanses My peace would come to me. I came at last to the ocean And found it wild and black, And I cried to the windless valleys, "Be kind and take me back!" But the thirsty tide ran inland, And the salt waves drank of me, And I who was fresh as the rainfall Am bitter as the sea.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to roll down the hill and laugh. They saw a big cage with a tiger inside. The tiger was impressive. It had orange and black stripes and sharp teeth.

"Wow, look at the tiger!" Lily said. "It is so big and strong!"

"Let's go closer and say hello," Ben said. "Maybe it is friendly."

They ran to the cage and waved at the tiger. The tiger growled and looked at them with hungry eyes.

"Hello, tiger!" Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The tiger did not want to play. It wanted to eat. It saw a hole in the cage and pushed it open. It jumped out and ran towards Lily and Ben.

"Help! Help!" Lily and Ben screamed. "The tiger is coming!"

They tried to run away, but they were too slow. The tiger caught them and bit them. They cried and hurt. The tiger was not friendly. It was mean and scary.

The end.

Once upon a time there were two very good friends named Jack and Jill. 

Jack was very excited when he saw a colorful magazine on the floor. He picked it up and rushed over to Jill, who was playing with some dolls.

"Look what I found," Jack said as he showed the magazine to Jill. 

Jill was very happy when she saw the magazine. She grabbed it from Jack and started flipping through it. Jack watched her in excitement. Suddenly, Jill raised her voice and exclaimed "wow!" 

Both of them started to yell for joy when Jill noticed a colorful picture of a butterfly on one of the pages. They both couldn't believe their luck. They took turns looking at the magazine and yelling with excitement.

Tina was a young girl who had a special secret. Every week she would store up her pocket money and use it to buy something special. One Monday morning, Tina decided to go to the store and see what she could get with her week's pocket money. After looking at lots of toys and treats, she finally chose a pretty rubber duck. 

When she got home she showed it to her mum who smiled. Tina hugged the duck tightly and played with it every day. Every week she would save up her pocket money and look forward to her next trip to the store. 

Over time, the rubber duck became Tina's special friend. It went wherever she went and she was so proud of it. Life was much more fun when it was around. Tina loved going to the store each week to see what new treasures she could find.

Today was a special day for Jane. She was going to school for the first time! She jumped out of bed and got dressed quickly. 
Jane's mom helped her prepare for school by packing her bag with lunch and her favourite toy. Jane was so excited she could hardly stand still!

When they arrived at school, they went to the classroom. Jane walked in and saw lots of new faces. She waved and smiled at them all. 
The teacher was very impatient and started talking right away. She explained the rules of the classroom and showed the children where they should sit. 
Jane looked around and saw the other children drawing and playing games. She could hardly wait to join in. 

Finally, it was time for the class to end. Jane said goodbye to the teacher and her new friends. She was happy that her first day of school went so well!

content: The press of the Spoon River Clarion was wrecked, And I was tarred and feathered, For publishing this on the day the Anarchists were hanged in Chicago: "I saw a beautiful woman with bandaged eyes Standing on the steps of a marble temple. Great multitudes passed in front of her, Lifting their faces to her imploringly. In her left hand she held a sword. She was brandishing the sword, Sometimes striking a child, again a laborer, Again a slinking woman, again a lunatic. In her right hand she held a scale; Into the scale pieces of gold were tossed By those who dodged the strokes of the sword. A man in a black gown read from a manuscript: 'She is no respecter of persons.' Then a youth wearing a red cap Leaped to her side and snatched away the bandage. And lo, the lashes had been eaten away From the oozy eye-lids; The eye-balls were seared with a milky mucus; The madness of a dying soul Was written on her face i But the multitude saw why she wore the bandage."

Jack was happily balancing his tomato on his head when he noticed something strange. He saw a filthy puddle on the ground! He asked his Mom questions that only a 3 year old would think to ask.

"Mom, what's that filthy stuff on the ground?"

His Mom smiled and said, "That's mud, Jack! It gets on the ground when it rains."

Jack exclaimed, "Wow, I like balancing my tomato, but I guess I won't balance it here. I don't want it to get filthy, too!"

So Jack put the tomato in his pocket and went inside to have some lunch. He was happy to have the tomato close by, and he never forgot to be careful with it. From then on, he only balanced the tomato in clean places!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily's friend Jack slipped on a banana peel and hurt his leg. He needed an operation to make it better.

Lily was worried about her friend, so she went to visit him in the hospital. Jack was sleeping, but his mom was there. Lily asked, "Is Jack going to be okay?" His mom said, "Yes, he just needs a modest operation to fix his leg."

Lily was happy to hear that Jack would be okay. She gave him a big hug and said, "I'm glad you'll be all better soon!" Jack smiled and said, "Thanks, Lily. You're a good friend."

Now we have met, we have look'd, we are safe, Return in peace to the ocean my love, I too am part of that ocean, my love, we are not so much separated, Behold the great rondure, the cohesion of all, how perfect! But as for me, for you, the irresistible sea is to separate us, As for an hour carrying us diverse, yet cannot carry us diverse forever; Be not impatient - a little space - know you I salute the air, the ocean and the land, Every day at sundown for your dear sake, my love.

Lily and Tom are playing in the park. They like to run and jump and slide. They see a big tree with many roots. The roots are like long arms that come out of the ground.

"Let's play hide and seek!" Lily says. "You count to ten and I hide. Then you find me."

"OK!" Tom says. He closes his eyes and starts to count. "One, two, three..."

Lily runs to the tree and looks for a good spot. She sees a big root that makes a hole under the tree. She crawls inside and giggles. She thinks Tom will never find her there.

"Ten!" Tom says. He opens his eyes and looks around. He sees the slide, the swings, the bench, but he does not see Lily. He runs to the tree and looks behind it. He does not see Lily. He looks up at the branches. He does not see Lily. He looks under the roots. He sees a pair of feet.

"I found you!" Tom says. He pulls Lily out of the hole. Lily laughs and rubs her head. She feels dizzy from being upside down.

"That was a good hiding spot!" Tom says. "But I am good at finding!"

"Let's play again!" Lily says. "This time I count and you hide!"

They run to the tree and start a new game. They have fun playing hide and seek with the roots.

One day, a girl named Lily went to play outside. She saw an ugly, old mill near her house. Lily liked to pretend, so she made up a story about the mill. In her story, the mill was a big castle.

Lily met a boy named Max. Max was playing near the mill too. "Let's pretend this mill is a big castle," said Lily to Max. Max liked Lily's idea, so they played together.

But then, a big wind came and blew the mill's door open. The wind scared Lily and Max. They did not want to play near the ugly mill anymore. They ran back to their homes and told their moms about the adventure.

Mia and Mommy went to the park together. Mommy brought a ball, but Mia wanted to play a new game. Mommy said, "We can organize a line of people!" Mia was glad to try something new. 

They made a line with Mommy and Mia at one end and a big tree at the other. Mommy threw the ball to Mia, who ran and caught it. Mia ran back and handed the ball to Mommy. Then Mommy threw it to someone else in the line. 

Everyone was having fun running back and forth from Mommy to the tree. They kept throwing the ball to each other until their feet were tired. Mia was glad she got to play a new game. 

They said goodbye to everyone and started walking back home. Mia and Mommy smiled at each other and held hands. They had a great time organizing the line of people.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl who liked fixing things. She was only three years old, but she was kind and knew a lot about how things worked. Every day, she would ask her parents for permission to work on different toys and machines. They would always say yes and smile as she twirled her screwdriver and fixed whatever needed to be done.

One day, the girl's mom took her to a mechanic shop. Inside, there were lots of car parts and tools everywhere. The girl was so excited to be there. Her parents said it was ok for her to explore, so she happily did just that. She used a small hammer and screwdriver to make the different car parts work better.

The girl was so brave that she forgot to be scared. She worked on the cars with the mechanic, fixing whatever problems they had. The mechanic was so impressed with her that he asked her to come back every day to help him out. She was so proud and said yes right away.

Every day after that, the girl was allowed to go to the mechanic shop and help out. She cheered up all the cars with her bravery and her tiny screwdrivers. Everyone was impressed with her hard work and she was very proud of what she could do. The brave little girl went on to become a great mechanic one day!

content: Afoot and light-hearted I take to the open road, Healthy, free, the world before me, The long brown path before me leading wherever I choose. Once upon a time there was a tiny mouse. Every day she explored her big world. One day she heard a strange noise. She froze! Her heart beat fast. She felt a funny urge to go see. 

As the mouse crept closer she shivered with fear. Suddenly a bright light shone through the darkness. She couldn't believe what she saw! There was an interesting box wrapped in a sparkly ribbon.

Slowly the mouse reached out to touch it. But just then the light faded away. She was all alone again. 

The mouse had an urge to open the box, so she slowly peeled away the ribbon. Inside was a glittery surprise! It was a sparkly crown fit for a tiny mouse king or queen. 

The mouse felt extra special wearing the crown. From that day on she knew that anything was possible if you had the courage to explore.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He had a favorite hat that he always wore. It was blue and had a big red star on it. Timmy loved his hat so much that he wore it everywhere he went. 

One day, Timmy met a girl named Sally. Sally had a sweet candy that she was eating. Timmy asked her if he could have some of the candy. Sally said, "Sure, but be careful not to break it." Timmy took a piece of the candy and put it in his mouth. It was the sweetest candy he had ever tasted. 

Suddenly, Timmy's hat fell off his head and onto the ground. Sally accidentally stepped on it and it broke. Timmy was very sad because his favorite hat was broken. He said to Sally, "You broke my hat! I don't like you anymore." Sally felt bad and said sorry, but Timmy didn't forgive her. 

From that day on, Timmy never wore a hat again. He always remembered the day when his favorite hat broke and how Sally ruined it. The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy who wanted to marry a cherry. He thought that this was a really delicious idea. The cherry heard about this and was so excited. She couldn't believe she was going to get married! 

The boy and the cherry talked about the marriage and made all the plans. On the day of the wedding, the boy put on his best clothes and the cherry put on her prettiest petals. They got married surrounded by their family and friends! 

The cherry was so happy to be married to the boy. She knew they would have lots of fun together. To celebrate their marriage they ate some delicious cherries. And they lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved looking at the stars at night and dreaming about visiting a planet one day. One night, she saw a shooting star and made a wish to visit a planet.

The next day, she met a wise old man who told her that visiting a planet was not possible. Lily felt gloomy and regretted making her wish. She asked the old man why she couldn't visit a planet, and he explained that it was too far away and too dangerous.

Lily felt sad, but the old man told her that she could still dream about the planets and imagine what it would be like to visit them. From that day on, Lily would look up at the stars and imagine herself flying through space, visiting all the planets in the galaxy. She no longer felt gloomy and didn't regret making her wish anymore, because she realized that sometimes it's better to dream than to have everything you want.
