name_of_work: The Bay by James K. Baxter
content: One the road to the bay was a lake of rushes Where we bathed at times and changed in the bamboos. Now it is rather to stand and say How many roads we take that lead to Nowhere, The alley overgrown, no meaning now but loss: Not that veritable garden where everything comes easy. And by the bay itself were cliffs with carved names And a hut on the shore by the Maori ovens. We raced boats from the banks of the pumice creek Or swam in those autumnal shallows Growing cold in amber water, riding the logs Upstream, and waiting for the taniwha. So now I remember the bay and the little spiders On driftwood, so poisonous and quick. The carved cliffs and the great outcrying surf With currents round the rocks and the birds rising. A thousand times an hour is torn across And burned for the sake of going on living. But I remember the bay that never was And stand like stone and cannot turn away.

I have a word for it -- the way the surface waited all day to be a silvery pause between sky and city -- which is elver. And another one for how the bay shelved cirrus clouds piled up at the edge of the Irish Sea, which is elver too. The old Blackrock baths have been neglected now for fifty years, fine cracks in the tiles visible as they never were when I can I can I can shouted Harry Vernon as he dived from the highest board curving down into salt and urine his cry fading out through the half century it took to hear as a child that a glass eel had been seen entering the seawater baths at twilight -- also known as elver -- and immediately the word begins a delicate migration -- a fine crazing healing in the tiles -- the sky deepening above a city that has always been unsettled between sluice gates and the Irish Sea to which there now comes at dusk a translucent visitor yearning for the estuary.

name_of_work: Your Attention Please by Peter Porter
content: The Polar DEW has just warned that A nuclear rocket strike of At least one thousand megatons Has been launched by the enemy Directly at our major cities. This announcement will take Two and a quarter minutes to make, You therefore have a further Eight and a quarter minutes To comply with the shelter Requirements published in the Civil Defence Code - section Atomic Attack. A specially shortened Mass Will be broadcast at the end Of this announcement- Protestant and Jewish services Will begin simultaneously- Select your wavelength immediately According to instructions In the Defence Code. Do not Take well-loved pets (including birds) Into your shelter - they will consume Fresh air. Leave the old and bed- ridden, you can do nothing for them. Remember to press the sealing Switch when everyone is in The shelter. Set the radiation Aerial, turn on the geiger barometer. Turn off your television now. Turn off your radio immediately The Services end. At the same time Secure explosion plugs in the ears Of each member of your family. Take Down your plasma flasks. Give your children The pills marked one and two In the C.D. green container, then put Them to bed. Do not break The inside airlock seals until The radiation All Clear shows (Watch for the cuckoo in your perspex panel), or your District Touring Doctor rings your bell. If before this, your air becomes Exhausted or if any of your family Is critically injured, administer The capsules marked 'Valley Forge' (Red pocket in No. 1 Survival Kit) For painless death. (Catholics Will have been instructed by their priests What to do in this eventuality.) This announcement is ending. Our President Has already given orders for Massive retaliation - it will be Decisive. Some of us may die. Remember, statistically It is not likely to be you. All flags are flying fully dressed On Government buildings - the sun is shining. Death is the least we have to fear. We are all in the hands of God, Whatever happens happens by His Will. Now go quickly to your shelters.

Lila and Ben are playing with their vehicles on the floor. Lila has a red car and Ben has a blue truck. They make noises as they drive them around.

"Vroom, vroom, I'm going to the park!" Lila says.

"Honk, honk, I'm going to the store!" Ben says.

They have fun until they see a big puzzle on the table. It has many pieces and a picture of a farm.

"Wow, look at that puzzle!" Lila says. "Can we do it?"

"Sure, let's try!" Ben says.

They leave their vehicles on the floor and go to the table. They pick up some pieces and try to fit them together.

"This piece goes here, see?" Lila says, showing Ben a piece with a cow.

"No, it doesn't, it goes here!" Ben says, taking the piece from Lila and putting it in another spot.

They start to argue and pull the pieces from each other.

"Give it back, that's mine!" Lila says.

"No, it's mine, you're wrong!" Ben says.

They get angry and snap at each other.

"Stop it, you're mean!" Lila says.

"No, you stop it, you're silly!" Ben says.

They hear a loud noise from the floor. They look and see their vehicles smashed and broken. They forgot to put them away and stepped on them.

"Oh no, our vehicles!" Lila says.

"They're ruined!" Ben says.

They feel sad and sorry. They look at each other and say:

"I'm sorry, I didn't mean to snap at you."

"I'm sorry, too, I didn't mean to snap at you."

They hug and make up. They decide to share the puzzle and help each other. They also decide to take care of their vehicles and put them away when they're done.

They learn to be nice and have fun together.

Once there was a bear named Bob. He loved to throw parties. Today was the day of his biggest party yet! 

Bob invited all of his friends over for dinner. When everyone arrived, Bob served a big bowl of salad. Everyone clapped and applauded Bob for making such a delicious dinner. 

Bob's friend Sam said, "This salad is so dry! I need something to make it wetter." Bob reached into his cupboard and pulled out a bottle of oil. Everyone laughed and applauded Bob again. 

Bob poured the oil onto the salad, and it became more juicy and wet. Everyone enjoyed the salad and the party. 

In the end, Bob bowed graciously and everyone applauded him one last time.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful little girl. Her name was Jane. One day, she went outside to play. Suddenly, she saw a stranger. She was scared. Jane didn't know what to do.

But then, the stranger smiled. He held out his hands and said â€œhello, I'm Tom. Would you like to come play with me?â€ Jane was still scared, but something about Tom made her feel safe. She smiled and said yes.

Tom and Jane played together for the rest of the day. When it was time to go home, Jane gave Tom a big hug and said goodbye. She was sad to leave him, but she knew she would see him again soon.

The next day, Tom was waiting for Jane when she came outside. Jane was so happy, she ran over and hugged him. As they played together again, Jane knew she had found a new friend. She loved playing with Tom.

Tom and Jane became the best of friends. Whenever Jane was feeling scared or sad, she knew she could count on Tom. He was her powerful, friendly stranger and she loved him.

name_of_work: The Forced Recruit by Elizabeth Barrett Browning
content: In the ranks of the Austrian you found him, He died with his face to you all; Yet bury him here where around him You honour your bravest that fall. Venetian, fair-featured and slender, He lies shot to death in his youth, With a smile on his lips, over-tender For any mere soldier's dead mouth. No stranger, and yet not a traitor, Though alien the cloth on his breast; Underneath it how seldom a greater Young heart has a shot sent to rest! By your enemy tortured and goaded To march with them, stand in their file, His musket, see, never was loaded, He facing your guns with that smile! As orphans yearn on to their mothers, He yearned to your patriot bands;-- "Let me die for our Italy, brothers, If not in your ranks, by your hands!" "Aim straightly, fire steady, spare me A ball in the body which may Deliver my heart here, and tear me This badge of the Austrian away!" So thought he, so died he this morning. What then? many others have died. Ay, but easy for men to die scorning The death-stroke, who fought side by side-- One tricolor floating above them; Struck down 'mid triumphant acclaims Of an Italy rescued to love them And blazon the brass with their names. But he, without witness or honour, There, shamed in his country's regard, With the tyrants who march in upon her, Died faithful and passive--'twas hard. 'Twas sublime. In a cruel restriction Cut off from the guerdon of sons, With most filial obedience, conviction, His soul kissed the lips of her guns. That moves you? Nay, grudge not to show it, While digging a grave for him here: The others who died, says your poet, Have glory,--let him have a tear.

name_of_work: Hug O' War by Shel Silverstein
content: I will not play at tug o' war. I'd rather play at hug o' war, Where everyone hugs Instead of tugs, Where everyone giggles And rolls on the rug, Where everyone kisses, And everyone grins, And everyone cuddles, And everyone wins.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to ride his bike. Every day, he put on his helmet and went outside to play. His helmet was very important. It kept his head safe.

One warm day, Tim met a new friend named Sam. Sam was riding his bike too. They decided to play together. They had lots of fun riding their bikes up and down the street.

"Listen," said Tim to Sam, "we must always wear our helmets when we ride our bikes. It keeps us safe." Sam nodded and said, "Yes, we should always listen to our moms and dads when they tell us to wear our helmets."

So Tim and Sam rode their bikes together, always wearing their helmets. They had lots of fun and stayed safe. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play pretend with her toys. One day, she found a toy telescope and looked through it. She saw a beautiful sight of stars and planets.

Lily pretended she was an astronaut and flew to space in her imagination. She had a perfect time exploring the universe. But as she was getting ready to come back to Earth, she accidentally broke the telescope.

Lily was very sad and knew she had to tell her mom. When she did, her mom was upset but forgave her. From then on, Lily learned to be more careful with her toys and to always tell the truth.

Once upon a time there was a mysterious scooter. It shined very bright, like a diamond and it had an amazing design. Everyday, the scooter went around the neighborhood making noise and children all around the street loved looking at it. 

One day, a three year old boy called Jax saw the scooter and he got really excited. He wanted to be able to ride the scooter, but it was too big for his small feet. But Jax never gave up and he always pointed to the scooter when it went by.

One day, Jax was out playing with his friends when suddenly he saw the scooter parked next to the park. He started running towards it and he couldn't believe his eyes! The mysterious scooter was his!

He hopped on and he scooted around the park for hours and hours. He felt so incredibly happy! From that day, Jax and his scooter were never apart and he would always point to it whenever he saw it proudly!

name_of_work: Summer Morn in New Hampshire by Claude McKay
content: All yesterday it poured, and all night long I could not sleep; the rain unceasing beat Upon the shingled roof like a weird song, Upon the grass like running children's feet. And down the mountains by the dark cloud kissed, Like a strange shape in filmy veiling dressed, Slid slowly, silently, the wraith-like mist, And nestled soft against the earth's wet breast. But lo, there was a miracle at dawn! The still air stirred at touch of the faint breeze, The sun a sheet of gold bequeathed the lawn, The songsters twittered in the rustling trees. And all things were transfigured in the day, But me whom radiant beauty could not move; For you, more wonderful, were far away, And I was blind with hunger for your love.

Once upon a time there was a little bear named Bob. He was very excited for breakfast today because his mom had made some special toast. Every morning she cut slices of delicious toast and smothered them in honey and butter.

Bob jumped out of bed and went straight to the kitchen. He was thrilled when he saw that his mom had made the special toast. She said, "Oh my gosh, look at you. You're so excited for this toast!"

Bob sat down and eagerly took a bite. He smiled with delight. Suddenly, he felt something wet and warm on his paw. He looked down and saw that he had dropped the toast on the floor! His mom said, "It's ok, Bob. Go ahead and get some more toast." 

So, Bob went straight to the counter, grabbed a slice of toast and took another bite. He was so excited to eat all of the yummy toast. Bob loved it so much that he wanted to get some more. He finished up his second slice and smiled, knowing he would get to eat more delicious toast.

Once upon a time there was a green frog. The frog wanted a place to live and he looked around, but he couldn't find anything.

The frog saw a bird in the sky and asked if he could help. The bird said, "Yes, come with me." The frog hopped and jumped and eventually they arrived at a quiet pond.

The frog looked around and saw that he was not alone! There were other frogs in the pond too and they welcomed the new frog with open arms.

The new frog was so happy to be in his new home. He made friends and even learnt how to stretch his legs to help him jump higher and swim faster.

The little frog loved his new home and was so glad that he had been welcomed. And he lived happily ever after in the peaceful, green pond.

In late winter I sometimes glimpse bits of steam coming up from some fault in the old snow and bend close and see it is lung-colored and put down my nose and know the chilly, enduring odor of bear. I take a wolf's rib and whittle it sharp at both ends and coil it up and freeze it in blubber and place it out on the fairway of the bears. And when it has vanished I move out on the bear tracks, roaming in circles until I come to the first, tentative, dark splash on the earth. And I set out running, following the splashes of blood wandering over the world. At the cut, gashed resting places I stop and rest, at the crawl-marks where he lay out on his belly to overpass some stretch of bauchy ice I lie out dragging myself forward with bear-knives in my fists. On the third day I begin to starve, at nightfall I bend down as I knew I would at a turd sopped in blood, and hesitate, and pick it up, and thrust it in my mouth, and gnash it down, and rise and go on running. On the seventh day, living by now on bear blood alone, I can see his upturned carcass far out ahead, a scraggled, steamy hulk, the heavy fur riffling in the wind. I come up to him and stare at the narrow-spaced, petty eyes, the dismayed face laid back on the shoulder, the nostrils flared, catching perhaps the first taint of me as he died. I hack a ravine in his thigh, and eat and drink, and tear him down his whole length and open him and climb in and close him up after me, against the wind, and sleep. And dream of lumbering flatfooted over the tundra, stabbed twice from within, splattering a trail behind me, splattering it out no matter which way I lurch, no matter which parabola of bear-transcendence, which dance of solitude I attempt, which gravity-clutched leap, which trudge, which groan. Until one day I totter and fall-- fall on this stomach that has tried so hard to keep up, to digest the blood as it leaked in, to break up and digest the bone itself: and now the breeze blows over me, blows off the hideous belches of ill-digested bear blood and rotted stomach and the ordinary, wretched odor of bear, blows across my sore, lolled tongue a song or screech, until I think I must rise up and dance. And I lie still. I awaken I think. Marshlights reappear, geese come trailing again up the flyway. In her ravine under old snow the dam-bear lies, licking lumps of smeared fur and drizzly eyes into shapes with her tongue. And one hairy-soled trudge stuck out before me, the next groaned out, the next, the next, the rest of my days I spend wandering: wondering what, anyway, was that sticky infusion, that rank flavor of blood, that poetry, by which I lived?

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They had a lot of fun with their toys and their dog. They made a big mess with the mud and the water.

"Tom, Lily, time to come inside!" their mom called from the door. "You need to wash your hands and have a snack."

Tom and Lily ran to the door. They were hungry and thirsty. But they forgot something very important.

"Mom, I need to go to the toilet!" Lily said when they got inside.

"Me too!" Tom said.

"OK, hurry up then. The toilet is over there." their mom said, pointing to the bathroom.

Tom and Lily ran to the bathroom. But there was a problem. There was only one toilet and they both wanted to use it.

"I was here first!" Tom said, pushing Lily away.

"No, you were not! I was here first!" Lily said, pushing Tom back.

They started to fight and shout. They were very angry with each other. They did not want to share the toilet.

Their mom heard the noise and came to the bathroom. She saw Tom and Lily fighting and the toilet seat broken.

"What are you doing?" she asked, very angry. "Why are you fighting over the toilet? You know you have to share and wait your turn."

Tom and Lily stopped fighting. They looked at their mom and the toilet. They felt bad. They remembered that they had to be nice to each other and not break things.

"Sorry, mom." Tom said.

"Sorry, mom." Lily said.

They hugged their mom and said sorry to each other. They took turns to use the toilet and washed their hands. Then they had a snack and played nicely in the living room. They did not fight over the toilet again.

For marriage, love and love alone's the argument. Sweet ceremony, then hand in hand we go Taking to our changed, still dangerous days, our complement. We think we know ourselves, but all we know Is: love surprises us. It's like when sunlight flings A sudden shaft that lights up glamorous the rain Across a Glasgow street - or when Botanic Spring's First crisp, dry breath turns February air champagne. Delight's infectious - your friends Put on, with glad rag finery today, your joy, Renew in themselves the right true ends They won't let old griefs, old lives, destroy. When at our lover's feet our opened selves we've laid We find ourselves, and all the world, remade.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk in the park with her mom and dad. One day, they saw a big wardrobe in the park. Lily's mom said, "I wish we had a wardrobe like that at home." Lily looked at the wardrobe and felt envious.

The next day, when Lily woke up, she saw a big box in front of her room. She asked her mom, "What is inside the box?" Her mom said, "Why don't you open it and see?" Lily opened the box and saw a beautiful wardrobe inside. She was so happy and said, "I can't wait to put my clothes in it and show it to my friends!"

Lily's mom smiled and said, "Remember the wardrobe we saw in the park? Your dad and I bought it for you." Lily was so surprised and hugged her mom and dad. From that day on, Lily walked around the park with a big smile on her face, feeling grateful for her new wardrobe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play dress-up and wear his favorite superhero costume. One day, Timmy's friend came over and they decided to play together. Timmy's friend wanted to wear Timmy's superhero costume, but Timmy didn't want to share. 

Timmy's friend felt sad and left Timmy's house. Timmy felt guilty for not sharing his costume and wanted to make it up to his friend. Timmy decided to take his superhero costume to his friend's house and give it to him as a gift. 

When Timmy's friend saw the costume, he felt very happy and they both played together wearing their superhero costumes. Timmy learned that it's important to share and not to feel guilty when you make a mistake.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat her breakfast on a shiny plate that sparkled in the sun. One day, she was eating her cereal when her mom came into the room.

"Wow, Lily! That plate is incredible! Where did you get it?" her mom asked.

"I got it from the store," Lily replied. "It shines so bright in the morning sun."

Her mom smiled and said, "I think it's time for a new plate for me too."

Once there was an old octopus who lived deep in the sea. She had been there for a long, long time and was very lonely. One day an old ship sailed over her and she was very scared. Suddenly the ship got stuck and started to sink!

The old octopus was determined to rescue the people on the ship. She used all her strength and managed to pull the ship away from danger. When she was done, the people were very thankful and cheered.

The old octopus was very happy that she had been able to rescue the people on the ship. From then on, the old octopus was known to be a hero.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. Jack had a very important job and he was very proud of it. He wanted everyone to know about it, so he decided to tell Jill all about it.

"I have the most important job", said Jack.
"What sort of job?" asked Jill.
"I am an astronaut", replied Jack.
Jill felt a bit sad and jealous. She thought her job was not as important as Jack's.

Then Jack said something very kind.
"It's okay, my job is very important, but so is yours. You help people and that's very important too," said Jack.

Jill smiled, she felt better and proud of her job.

The moral of this story is that everyone has an important job in this world. Whether it's small or big, it is always important in its own way.

Once upon a time, there was a caterpillar who was very dirty. He was so filthy that no one wanted to be his friend. One day, he decided he wanted to clean himself up. He saw the wind folding the leaves of a nearby tree and decided that he could do the same.

So the caterpillar started folding the leaves around him. He folded the leaves around his entire body until he was all clean! He was very proud of himself and suddenly, his friends noticed how shiny and clean he was!

They were so impressed that they all agreed to be his friends. He was so happy and thankful to have his caterpillar friends to play with. From then on, the caterpillar kept himself very clean, always folding the leaves around him.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. He was very independent and liked to do things by himself. One day, he was walking in the jungle when he met a little monkey. The monkey said, "Hello, Mr. Elephant! Where are you going?"

The elephant replied, "I am going to find some food."

The monkey said, "Can I come with you?"

The elephant thought about it and said, "Sure, you can come with me. But you have to be careful."

The monkey was happy and they walked together. They found some bananas and the elephant said, "These bananas are for us to share."

The monkey said, "Thank you, Mr. Elephant. You are very kind."

The elephant smiled and said, "It's always nice to share with friends."

Once upon a time, there was a princess named Lily. She was very spoiled and always got what she wanted. One day, she asked her mother, the queen, for a golden crown with diamonds. Her mother said yes and gave her the crown.

While walking in the garden, Lily saw a butterfly. She admired its colorful wings and followed it. Suddenly, she fell into a deep hole. She called for help, but no one heard her.

Days passed, and the queen searched for her daughter everywhere. She found the hole and heard Lily's voice. She quickly rescued her. Lily learned her lesson and realized that she should not be spoiled. She admired her mother's love and promised to be a good princess.

Once upon a time there was a girl, who loved to wander in the woods. She was always curious to explore, and loved to find new things.

One day, the girl went really deep into the woods and came across a big, tall cliff. She had never seen anything like it before. She stopped to take a look, and it looked so lovely with the light shining on it.

Just then, the girl heard a voice; it was coming from the top of the cliff! She squinted, and saw a little old man sitting at the top. He was looking down at her, and asked, â€œWhat are you doing here?â€

The girl said she was out wandering, and looking for new things. The old man smiled and said, â€œWell, thereâ€™s plenty to explore up here. Come on up and join me!â€

The girl was a bit scared, but with some courage and a helping hand from the old man, she was able to climb up the cliff.

At the top, it was so nice and light, and the old man showed her many things. They talked and laughed until the sun began to set, and they went back down the cliff together. 

The girl kept coming back to that cliff, often with the old man, and they would continue to explore and wander for hours.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Maggie. Maggie was always very proud of her room. She had lots of bright colourful toys and her bed was made out with her very best blanket.

Today Maggie was feeling extra proud. She had been busy tidying up and had just replaced the old sheet with a fresh clean one.

Maggie looked around her room, happy with her hard work. "My room looks beautiful now!" she said to herself.

Just then, Maggie's brother James came in. He saw the new sheet on the bed and walked up to it. "I'm going to jump on that sheet!" he said excitedly.

Maggie felt angry. "No!", she shouted. "That's my sheet! You can't go near it!"

James frowned. "But why not?", he asked.

Maggie smiled. She proudly explained that she had worked hard to make her room look nice. She was happy with how it looked and didn't want anything to ruin it!

James understood and went off to find something else to do. Maggie smiled and hugged her sheet. She was very proud of her work, and she knew that nobody was going to replace it now.

Sam was feeling very jolly on Wednesday. He put on his favourite blue t-shirt and ran to the park. When he arrived, he saw his friend Sue.

"Hi!" Sam said, smiling.

"Hi Sam, why are you so jolly?" Sue asked.

"It's Wednesday and I can wear my favourite t-shirt," Sam replied.

Sue smiled. "Let's play tag!"

So the two friends ran around the park, laughing and being jolly together. They played for hours, until it was time to go home.

"Bye Sam!" Sue said as she waved goodbye.

"Bye Sue," Sam replied. "I had a jolly Wednesday!"

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim had a secret. He found a weird ice cream cone. It was not like other ice creams. This one could talk!

The ice cream said, "Hello, Tim! I can be any flavor you want, but you must eat me fast, or I will melt!" Tim was very happy. He loved ice cream. He wished for a yummy chocolate flavor.

Tim ate the ice cream very fast, so it did not melt. He told his friends about the weird ice cream cone. They all wanted to find one too. But it was Tim's special secret. And he smiled every time he thought about it.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to zoom around on his bike. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy said, "I dare you to ride your bike down the big hill!" Timmy was scared, but he wanted to be brave. So, he rode down the hill as fast as he could.

At the bottom of the hill, Timmy crashed into a tree. His bike was broken and he hurt his arm. Timmy's mom took him to the hospital. The doctor said that Timmy's arm was broken and it would take a while to heal. Timmy was sad because he couldn't zoom around on his bike like normal.

Timmy learned that sometimes it's not good to do things just because someone dares you to. He also learned that it's important to be careful and not take unnecessary risks. From then on, Timmy made sure to always wear his helmet and be safe when riding his bike.

Sara liked to draw with crayons. She drew flowers, animals, and houses. She wanted to improve her drawing, so she asked her mom for help.

"Mom, can you teach me how to draw better?" Sara said.

"Sure, honey. Let me see what you have." Mom said. She looked at Sara's drawings and smiled. "You are very creative, Sara. I like your colors and shapes. But do you want to learn some new skills?"

"Yes, Mom. I want to improve." Sara said.

"Okay, then. Let's use some newspaper. Newspaper is good for drawing because it is big and cheap. You can draw on both sides. And you can use a pencil instead of crayons. Pencil is good for drawing because you can erase and change your lines. Do you want to try?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom. That sounds fun." Sara said.

Mom gave Sara some newspaper and a pencil. She showed Sara how to draw a circle, a square, a triangle, and a star. She also showed Sara how to draw a face, a body, and a tree. Sara followed Mom's instructions and tried to copy her drawings. She found it hard at first, but she did not give up. She erased and tried again. She asked Mom for feedback and tips. She practiced and practiced.

After a while, Sara had a lot of drawings on the newspaper. She was proud of her work. She showed Mom her drawings and said, "Look, Mom. I improved. I can draw better now. Thank you for teaching me."

Mom hugged Sara and said, "You're welcome, Sara. I'm proud of you too. You improved a lot. You worked hard and learned new skills. That's how you grow and achieve your goals. Remember, drawing is fun, but it is also hard. You have to practice and be patient. But if you do, you will improve and enjoy it more."

Sara nodded and smiled. She learned a valuable lesson. She learned that hard work pays off. She learned that improvement is possible. She learned that Mom is a good teacher. She learned that she loves drawing.

The tree that never had to fight For sun and sky and air and light, But stood out in the open plain And always got its share of rain, Never became a forest king But lived and died a scrubby thing. The man who never had to toil To gain and farm his patch of soil, Who never had to win his share Of sun and sky and light and air, Never became a manly man But lived and died as he began. Good timber does not grow with ease, The stronger wind, the stronger trees, The further sky, the greater length, The more the storm, the more the strength. By sun and cold, by rain and snow, In trees and men good timbers grow. Where thickest lies the forest growth We find the patriarchs of both. And they hold counsel with the stars Whose broken branches show the scars Of many winds and much of strife. This is the common law of life.

Once upon a time, there lived a big beetle in a pond.

When the beetle wanted to go somewhere, it would swim. Every day, the beetle swam around the pond, exploring and having fun.

One day, a 3 year old girl named Mary saw the big beetle swimming around in the pond. She was amazed and decided to talk to it.

"Hello beetle! What are you doing?" she asked. The beetle replied with a cheerful "I'm swimming!"

Mary smiled and said, "Can I join you?"
The beetle was happy and said, "Sure!"

So, Mary and the big beetle swam around the pond together. They had lots of fun and enjoyed their time together. 

When it was time to go home, Mary gave the beetle a hug, said goodbye and went on her way. The beetle waved and watched Mary until she was out of sight. After that, the big beetle swam back to his pond and continued exploring.

Helmet and rifle, pack and overcoat Marched through a forest. Somewhere up ahead Guns thudded. Like the circle of a throat The night on every side was turning red. They halted and they dug. They sank like moles Into the clammy earth between the trees. And soon the sentries, standing in their holes, Felt the first snow. Their feet began to freeze. At dawn the first shell landed with a crack. Then shells and bullets swept the icy woods. This lasted many days. The snow was black. The corpses stiffened in their scarlet hoods. Most clearly of that battle I remember The tiredness in eyes, how hands looked thin Around a cigarette, and the bright ember Would pulse with all the life there was within.

Once upon a time, there was a pot. It was a very special pot, because it was always lending things to people. One day, the pot was walking through the forest. Suddenly, a scary monster appeared! The monster wanted to borrow the pot, but the pot was very scared.

The pot tried to run away, but he was too slow. The monster caught the pot, and he wouldn't let it go. He said he needed the pot to make a soup. So the pot decided to lend the monster the pot, even though it was very scared.

The monster thanked the pot and put it in his pocket. Then he made a delicious soup in the pot. The monster waved goodbye to the pot, and the pot was so happy to get to go free. From that day on, the pot remembered to be brave, even when scary things happen. The pot kept lending things to people - it was brave and kind.

name_of_work: Mundus Et Infans by W.H. Auden
content: A cloudless night like this Can set the spirit soaring; After a tiring day The clockwork spectacle is Impressive in a slightly boring Eighteenth-century way. It soothed adolescence a lot To meet so shameless a stare; The things I did could not Be as shocking as they said If that would still be there After the shocked were dead. Now, unready to die But already at the stage When one starts to dislike the young, I am glad those points in the sky May also be reckoned among The creatures of middle-age. It's cosier thinking of night As more an Old People's Home Than a shed for a faultless machine, That the red pre-Cambrian light Is gone llke Imperial Rome Or myself at seventeen. Yet however much we may like The stoic manner in which The classical authors wrote, Only the young and the rich Have the nerve or the figure to strike The lacrimae rerum note. For this moment stalks abroad Like the last, and its wronged again Whimper and are ignored, And the truth cannot be hid; Somebody chose their pain, What needn't have happened did. Occurring this very night. By no established rule, Some event may already have hurled Its first little No at the right Of the laws we accept to school Our post-diluvian world: But the stars burn on overhead, Unconscious of final ends, As I walk home to bed, Asking what judgment waits My person, all my friends, And these United States.

Once upon a time there was a small gray mouse. It was always very quiet, but it wanted to go on an adventure. So one day, the mouse quit its home and went out in search of fun. 

Then, one day, it came across a strange toilet. It looked like a magical door! The mouse was curious and decided to enter. Once inside, it found a beautiful garden full of friends and fun. 

The mouse couldn't believe its eyes. It said, "Wow, this is the best adventure ever!" Then, the mouse said goodbye to its friends and quit the toilet. 

Finally, the mouse reached home, happy and full of stories to tell. It promised itself that it would never forget its magical adventure in the gray toilet.

name_of_work: Reflections on Having Left a Place of Retirement by Samuel Taylor Coleridge
content: Low was our pretty Cot: our tallest Rose Peep'd at the chamber-window. We could hear At silent noon, and eve, and early morn, The Sea's faint murmur. In the open air Our Myrtles blossom'd; and across the porch Thick Jasmins twined: the little landscape round Was green and woody, and refresh'd the eye. It was a spot which you might aptly call The Valley of Seclusion! Once I saw (Hallowing his Sabbath-day by quiteness) A wealthy son of Commerce saunter by, Bristowa's citizen: methought, it calm'd His thirst of idle gold, and made him muse With wiser feelings: for he paus'd, and look'd With a pleas'd sadness, and gaz'd all around, Then eyed our Cottage, and gaz'd round again, And sigh'd, and said, it was a Blessed Place. And we were bless'd. Oft with patient ear Long-listening to the viewless sky-lark's note (Viewless, or haply for a moment seen Gleaming on sunny wings) in whisper'd tones I said to my Beloved, `Such, sweet Girl! The inobtrusive song of Happiness, Unearthly minstrelsy! then only heard When the Soul seeks to hear ; when all is hush'd, And the Heart listens!' But the time, when first From that low Dell, steep up the stony Mount I climb'd with perilous toil and reach'd the top, Oh! what a goodly scene! Here the bleak mount, The bare bleak mountain speckled thin with sheep; Grey clouds, that shadowing spot the sunny fields; And river, now with bushy rocks o'er-brow'd, Now winding bright and full, with naked banks; And seats, and lawns, the Abbey and the wood, And cots, and hamlets, and faint city-spire; The Channel there, the Islands and white sails, Dim coasts, and cloud-like hills, and shoreless Ocean-- It seem'd like Omnipresence! God, methought, Had build him there a Temple: the whole World Seem'd imag'd in its vast circumference: No wish profan'd my overwhelmed heart. Blest hour! It was a luxury,--to be! Ah! quiet Dell! dear Cot, and Mount sublime! I was constrain'd to quit you. Was it right, While my unnumber'd brethren toil'd and bled, That I should dream away the entrusted hours On rose-leaf beds, pampering the coward heart With feelings all too delicate for use? Sweet is the tear that from some Howard's eye Drops on the cheek of one he lifts from earth: And he that works me good with unmov'd face, Does it but half: he chills me while he aids, My benefactor, not my brother man! Yet even this, this cold beneficience Praise, praise it, O my Soul! oft as thou scann'st The sluggard Pity's vision-weaving tribe! Who sigh for Wretchedness, yet shun the Wretched, Nursing in some delicious solitude Their slothful loves and dainty sympathies! I therefore go, and join head, heart, and hand, Active and firm, to fight the bloodless fight Of Science, Freedom, and the Truth in Christ. Yet oft when after honourable toil Rests the tir'd mind, and waking loves to dream, My spirit shall revisit thee, dear Cot! Thy Jasmin and thy window-peeping Rose, And Myrtles fearless of the mild sea-air. And I shall sigh fond wishes--sweet Abode! Ah!--had none greater! And that all had such! It might be so--but the time is not yet. Speed it, O Father! Let thy Kingdom come!

name_of_work: The Power of the Dog by Rudyard Kipling
content: There is sorrow enough in the natural way From men and women to fill our day; And when we are certain of sorrow in store, Why do we always arrange for more? Brothers and sisters, I bid you beware Of giving your heart to a dog to tear. Buy a pup and your money will buy Love unflinching that cannot lie Perfect passion and worship fed By a kick in the ribs or a pat on the head. Nevertheless it is hardly fair To risk your heart for a dog to tear. When the fourteen years which Nature permits Are closing in asthma, or tumour, or fits, And the vet's unspoken prescription runs To lethal chambers or loaded guns, Then you will find - it's your own affair, - But ... you've given your heart to a dog to tear. When the body that lived at your single will, With its whimper of welcome, is stilled (how still!), When the spirit that answered your every mood Is gone - wherever it goes - for good, You will discover how much you care, And will give your heart to a dog to tear! We've sorrow enough in the natural way, When it comes to burying Christian clay. Our loves are not given, but only lent, At compound interest of cent per cent, Though it is not always the case, I believe, That the longer we've kept 'em, the more do we grieve; For, when debts are payable, right or wrong, A short-time loan is as bad as a long - So why in - Heaven (before we are there) Should we give our hearts to a dog to tear?

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old. Jane had a secret. One day while walking in the park she found a yellow box with something hidden inside. She opened the box and found a big yellow balloon with a smiley face painted on it.

"Hello there," said Jane with a smile as she picked up the balloon.

The balloon giggled and said, "Hi Jane! I am so happy you found me. Will you take me home with you?"

Jane smiled and nodded her head. She and the balloon became best friends. Everywhere Jane went, the balloon followed. On sunny days they flew around the park, sparkling and smiling in the sunshine. On rainy days they curled up together and told stories.

Jane and the balloon were the very best of friends and they shared a special smile that never faded away.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sue. She was three years old. 

One day, Sue was playing in the garden when she found something very shiny and small. She went over for a closer look and saw that it was a button! She picked it up and started to play with it.

Suddenly, the button made a loud noise! It scared Sue and she screamed. But then she heard a voice say, "Don't be scared Sue, it's just me - the button!"

Sue was surprised and asked the button what it was doing there. The button introduced itself, saying it was looking for a new friend. Sue was very happy and said she could be its friend.

So every day Sue and the button would have wonderful adventures. They would have lots of fun playing games and singing songs. Sue loved her new friend, the loud button!

One day, Jack was in a special mood because it was his birthday. He looked around and smiled. Everyone was so special and nice to him. He had lots of presents, too.

Grandma gave him a small box. Inside were two shiny coins. She said, "These coins are useful. You can use them to buy something nice."

Jack was so excited. He shouted, "YAY!" and he shook them in his hand. He wanted to show them to everyone.

Dad said, "You can also shake them like this." He put them together and shook them to make a music sound. Jack shook them over and over, smiling and dancing. Everyone laughed and laughed.

It was the best birthday ever.

One day, Rhea couldn't find her favorite book. She looked high and low, but it was nowhere to be seen. She asked her mom and dad if they had seen it, but they said no. Rhea thought long and hard about where the book might be. Then, she had an idea.

She ran to the kitchen and opened the big freezer. Sure enough, her book was tucked inside. "How did it get there?", she wondered. Then she remembered that earlier, she had put it in the freezer to give it a nap. She had read that sometimes, books go to sleep when they get too tired.

Rhea carefully grabbed the book out of the freezer. It was a bit tough because it was so cold, but she was very careful. She hugged the book close and ran to her bedroom. She opened the book and the stories were back! She smiled, happy to have found her book.

John and his mom were at the store. John saw a big red cart and asked his mom if he could push it around. So his mom let him take the cart and John felt so excited. He happily pushed the cart around the store. 

When it was time to leave, John realized the cart was still with him. He didn't know what to do. He started to feel scared. But then someone came up to him, a store clerk. The clerk was so thoughtful and told John that he could keep the cart until he found his mom. 

John was so relieved and thanked the store clerk. He hurriedly pushed the cart around until he found his mom. His mom was so happy to see him and thanked the store clerk too. Everyone was so relieved the conflict was solved. 

John gave the cart back to the store clerk and they said goodbye. John was so happy to have such a thoughtful store clerk. He and his mom left the store with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a purple dress that she loved to wear. One day, she was playing with her toys when she noticed that her favorite cable was broken. She asked her mom to help her fix it. 

Her mom took out some tools and together they worked to complete the repair. Lily was so happy that her cable was fixed and she could play with her toys again. She hugged her mom and thanked her for helping her. 

From that day on, Lily made sure to take care of her cable so it wouldn't break again. She loved her purple dress and her toys, and was grateful for her mom who always helped her when she needed it.

Dark falls on this mid-western town where we once lived when myths collided. Dusk has hidden the bridge in the river which slides and deepens to become the water the hero crossed on his way to hell. Not far from here is our old apartment. We had a kitchen and an Amish table. We had a view. And we discovered there love had the feather and muscle of wings and had come to live with us, a brother of fire and air. We had two infant children one of whom was touched by death in this town and spared: and when the hero was hailed by his comrades in hell their mouths opened and their voices failed and there is no knowing what they would have asked about a life they had shared and lost. I am your wife. It was years ago. Our child was healed. We love each other still. Across our day-to-day and ordinary distances we speak plainly. We hear each other clearly. And yet I want to return to you on the bridge of the Iowa river as you were, with snow on the shoulders of your coat and a car passing with its headlights on: I see you as a hero in a text -- the image blazing and the edges gilded -- and I long to cry out the epic question my dear companion: Will we ever live so intensely again? Will love come to us again and be so formidable at rest it offered us ascension even to look at him? But the words are shadows and you cannot hear me. You walk away and I cannot follow

How doth the little crocodile Improve his shining tail, And pour the waters of the Nile On every golden scale! How cheerfully he seems to grin, How neatly spreads his claws, And welcomes little fishes in, With gently smiling jaws!

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Susan. She was 3 years old and went to a very fun playgroup. Her favourite thing about playgroup was the games, where she made lots of new friends.

Today, Susan was very troubled as she had been left at the school gates, and no one had come to collect her. Unsure of what to do, she began to weep.

Suddenly, a voice from behind said, "Don't cry little one, everything will be alright." Susan quickly turned to see a tall lady smiling at her. "My name is Miss Jones," she said. "I am the playgroup teacher. Welcome to the school."

Susan quickly ran to Miss Jones, who hugged her tightly. Miss Jones then said, "We can go inside now, it's time to head towards the exit."

The two of them walked through the school, hand in hand. Susan felt much calmer now that she was with someone. They waved to all the other children, who welcomed them.

Eventually, they arrived at the exit, and made their way out of school. Susan was relieved; she knew that everything would be alright.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mary. Mary was three years old. One day, Mary wanted to go to the park. She wanted to go into the park to play.

Mary asked her mom if she could go. Mom said yes. "But, be careful!" Mom cautioned.

So Mary went to the park. On her way, Mary saw a lot of traffic, but she was not afraid.

Finally, Mary arrived at the park. She saw a big pink slide. Mary was so excited! She ran to the slide and started to climb up, but it was too high.

Mary looked around and saw a small pink slide. She ran over and climbed up. She slide down again and again!

Mary decided to stay at the park and plan a picnic. She asked her mom to bring food and juice and they had a picnic in the park. 

Mary and Mom had a great time and when it was time to leave, they ran home together.

They laughed and talked and when they reached home they were both very happy!

One day, Mommy was very confused. She was looking for her bathrobe that she usually wears after taking a bath. She called for her 3 year old daughter and asked her if she had seen it. But the little girl just shook her head. 

Mommy began to look all around the house, but she couldn't find her bathrobe anywhere. Finally, she looked in her daughter's bedroom, and there it was, hanging on a little chair!

The little girl looked so happy to see her Mommy smiling. She said, "I miss you Mommy when I can't find you!" Mommy gave her a big hug and said, "I miss you too, sweetheart!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the world around her. One day, she found a small box in her backyard. She pulled it out of the ground and opened it. Inside, she found a tiny microscope.

Lily had never seen a microscope before, but she was very curious. She looked through the lens and saw something unknown. She called her mommy and said, "Mommy, come see! I found something unknown!"

Her mommy came over and looked through the microscope. "Wow, that's amazing!" she said. "What did you find?"

"I don't know," Lily said. "It's too small to see without the microscope. Can we pull out more things and look at them?"

"Of course!" her mommy said. They spent the rest of the day pulling out different things from the ground and looking at them through the microscope. It was a fun adventure for both of them.

name_of_work: A Limb Just Moved by Mirabai
content: You taught Your songs to the birds first, why was that? And You practised Your love in the hearts of animals before You created man, I know the planets talk at night and tell secrets about You. A limb just moved before me, the beauty of this world is causing me to weep

Jenny was getting ready to go for a drive, so she set up her vehicle. She was very careful and she strapped herself in.

"Where are we going?" asked Tommy, Jenny's 3-year old son.

"We're going to the park, Tommy," said Jenny, "it's a nice day today."

Tommy was excited to go. He waved goodbye to the family who had come to visit from out of town and watched out the window as they set off. Jenny was careful around all the corners and made sure to stop at the traffic lights.

Soon, they turned into the park. Tommy telephoned out in celebration when he spotted the playground. Jenny laughed and she set them off on a run, hand in hand.

The vehicle was soon parked and they sprinted over to the swings. Jenny gave Tommy a push and he laughed and laughed, flying high, higher and higher.

They finished off their morning with lunch in the picnic area and soon it was time to set off on the journey home. Jenny was careful on the return journey and soon they were back in the driveway.

Tommy gave Jenny a big hug, excited for their next adventure in the vehicle.

Oh! thou bright-beaming god, the plains are thirsting, Thirsting for freshening dew, and man is pining; Wearily move on thy horses-- Let, then, thy chariot descend! Seest thou her who, from ocean's crystal billows, Lovingly nods and smiles?--Thy heart must know her! Joyously speed on thy horses,-- Tethys, the goddess, 'tis nods! Swiftly from out his flaming chariot leaping, Into her arms he springs,--the reins takes Cupid,-- Quietly stand the horses, Drinking the cooling flood. Now from the heavens with gentle step descending, Balmy night appears, by sweet love followed; Mortals, rest ye, and love ye,-- Phoebus, the loving one, rests!

Once, there was a group of friends who all wanted to be on the same team. But they were scared to take the stand together and make their dream a reality.

One day, all their courage came out and they decided to take a stand. They formed a team and agreed to work together.

The team was so happy to be together, but then something scared them. A big, fierce animal came into the room!

The friends were so scared, but then they remembered something. They were a team and a team sticks together! So, all the friends grabbed hands and stood together against the animal.

The animal was so scared it ran away! Now the team is proud of themselves for taking a stand together, and for being brave enough to do it.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Benny. Benny loved to play all day, but sometimes he got tired. One day, Benny's mom said to him, "Benny, it's time for your nap. Lie down and relax."

Benny lay down on his bed and closed his eyes. He felt his chest go up and down as he breathed. His mom stroked his fur gently and said, "Just close your eyes and rest. You will feel better soon."

Benny smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy. Your gentle touch makes me feel happy." Benny slept for a while and woke up feeling refreshed. He hugged his mom and said, "I love you, Mommy. You always make me feel better."

Once upon a time, there was a powerful unicorn named Lily. Lily loved to move around the forest. Every morning, she galloped through the trees and over the hills.

One day, Lily stumbled upon a magical well. The well was filled with bright, glowing water. Lily started to move around the well. She drank some of the water and felt so strong and powerful.

Lily kept moving around the well, and soon enough, she saw something sparkle in the water. She moved closer and saw that it was a beautiful diamond!

Lily was so happy to have found such a powerful gem. She took the diamond, thanked the well and moved back through the forest. She brought the diamond back to her friends in the wood and everyone celebrated.

The end.

Oh would I could subdue the flesh Which sadly troubles me! And then perhaps could view the flesh As though I never knew the flesh And merry misery. To see the golden hiking girl With wind about her hair, The tennis-playing, biking girl, The wholly-to-my-liking girl, To see and not to care. At sundown on my tricycle I tour the Borough's edge, And icy as an icicle See bicycle by bicycle Stacked waiting in the hedge. Get down from me! I thunder there, You spaniels! Shut your jaws! Your teeth are stuffed with underwear, Suspenders torn asunder there And buttocks in your paws! Oh whip the dogs away my Lord, They make me ill with lust. Bend bare knees down to pray, my Lord, Teach sulky lips to say, my Lord, That flaxen hair is dust.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily wanted to sit down, but there were no chairs to use. She looked around and saw a big, easy chair in the corner of the room. She ran over to the chair and sat down. It was so comfortable! She decided she wanted to use the chair every day. The end.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit who wanted to find a new home. He decided to follow a butterfly that was flying across the meadow.

The butterfly flew from one flower to another, until it suddenly stopped. The rabbit followed and saw the beautiful butterfly resting on a soft green petal. The petal felt wet in the sun and suddenly the rabbit heard a loud splash. He looked up and realised there was a deep pond right beside him.

The rabbit was frightened and tried to escape. But no matter how much he hopped, he couldn't jump out of the pond. He was stuck and had to wait until someone came to help him. In the end, the rabbit learnt an important lesson: always be careful where you follow, especially when it looks tempting.

name_of_work: What's in it? by Vikram Seth
content: I heard your name the other day Mentioned by someone in a casual way. She said she thought that you were looking great. A waiter passed by with a plate. She reached out for a sandwich, and your name Went back from where it came. But like a serious owlet I stood there, Staring in mid-air. I frowned, then followed her around To hear, just once more, that sirenic sound - Those consonants, those vowels - what a fool! I show more circumspection as a rule. I love you more than I can say. Try as I do, it hasn't gone away. I hoped it would once, and I hope so still. Someday, I'm sure, it will. No glimpse, no news, no name will stir me then. But when? But when?

Down the close, darkening lanes they sang their way To the siding-shed, And lined the train with faces grimly gay. Their breasts were stuck all white with wreath and spray As men's are, dead. Dull porters watched them, and a casual tramp Stood staring hard, Sorry to miss them from the upland camp. Then, unmoved, signals nodded, and a lamp Winked to the guard. So secretly, like wrongs hushed-up, they went. They were not ours: We never heard to which front these were sent. Nor there if they yet mock what women meant Who gave them flowers. Shall they return to beatings of great bells In wild trainloads? A few, a few, too few for drums and yells, May creep back, silent, to still village wells Up half-known roads.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her pink scarf when it was cold outside. One day, she went outside to play in the snow.

Her friend, a wise old owl named Hootie, was sitting in a tree nearby. "Hello, Hootie!" Lily said. "Do you like my scarf?"

Hootie turned his head and looked at Lily's scarf. "I do indeed," he said. "It's very pretty. Did you know that you can bow with your scarf?"

Lily looked confused. "What do you mean, Hootie?"

Hootie flew down from the tree and showed Lily how to tie her scarf into a bow. Lily was so happy to learn something new. "Thank you, Hootie," she said. "You are very wise!"

Once upon a time, there was a litttle girl. She had black hair and black eyes and she was very brave. She wanted to explore the world.

One day she decided to find a well in the forest. She walked and walked until she finally found it. It was very deep and dark. She wanted to see how deep it was so she decided to throw a rock into the bottom.

The water was so dark that she couldn't see the bottom. She was scared, but she was excited too. She wanted to get to the bottom, so she decided not to quit.

She found a big black handkerchief in her pocket and tied it to a tree trunk. She held onto the end of it and stepped carefully into the well. Lower and lower she went, the handkerchief unwinding until she finally reached the bottom.

But it was dark and scary, and she was beginning to feel scared. She suddenly had the urge to quit and go back up, so she quickly let go of the handkerchief and started climbing back up.

When she reached the top, she was so relieved. She knew she had done the right thing and made the right decision to quit when she did.

--It seems a day (I speak of one from many singled out) One of those heavenly days that cannot die; When, in the eagerness of boyish hope, I left our cottage-threshold, sallying forth With a huge wallet o'er my shoulders slung, A nutting-crook in hand; and turned my steps Tow'rd some far-distant wood, a Figure quaint, Tricked out in proud disguise of cast-off weeds Which for that service had been husbanded, By exhortation of my frugal Dame-- Motley accoutrement, of power to smile At thorns, and brakes, and brambles,--and, in truth, More ragged than need was! O'er pathless rocks, Through beds of matted fern, and tangled thickets, Forcing my way, I came to one dear nook Unvisited, where not a broken bough Drooped with its withered leaves, ungracious sign Of devastation; but the hazels rose Tall and erect, with tempting clusters hung, A virgin scene!--A little while I stood, Breathing with such suppression of the heart As joy delights in; and, with wise restraint Voluptuous, fearless of a rival, eyed The banquet;--or beneath the trees I sate Among the flowers, and with the flowers I played; A temper known to those, who, after long And weary expectation, have been blest With sudden happiness beyond all hope. Perhaps it was a bower beneath whose leaves The violets of five seasons re-appear And fade, unseen by any human eye; Where fairy water-breaks do murmur on For ever; and I saw the sparkling foam, And--with my cheek on one of those green stones That, fleeced with moss, under the shady trees, Lay round me, scattered like a flock of sheep-- I heard the murmur, and the murmuring sound, In that sweet mood when pleasure loves to pay Tribute to ease; and, of its joy secure, The heart luxuriates with indifferent things, Wasting its kindliness on stocks and stones, And on the vacant air. Then up I rose, And dragged to earth both branch and bough, with crash And merciless ravage: and the shady nook Of hazels, and the green and mossy bower, Deformed and sullied, patiently gave up Their quiet being: and, unless I now Confound my present feelings with the past; Ere from the mutilated bower I turned Exulting, rich beyond the wealth of kings, I felt a sense of pain when I beheld The silent trees, and saw the intruding sky.-- Then, dearest Maiden, move along these shades In gentleness of heart; with gentle hand Touch--for there is a spirit in the woods.

name_of_work: As froth on the face of the deep by Christina Rossetti
content: As froth on the face of the deep, As foam on the crest of the sea, As dreams at the waking of sleep, As gourd of a day and a night, As harvest that no man shall reap, As vintage that never shall be, Is hope if it cling not aright, O my God, unto Thee.

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Tom. Tom was a foolish cat. He liked to play with a ball of yarn. One day, Tom saw a big knot in the yarn. He wanted to untie the knot.

As Tom played with the knot, he started to sneeze. He sneezed so much that his nose turned red. Tom did not stop playing with the knot. He thought it was fun to sneeze and play.

But Tom sneezed so much that he got sick. He felt very bad. Tom wished he had not played with the knot. In the end, Tom was still sick and could not play anymore.

name_of_work: Upon the Hearth the Fire is Red by J.R.R. Tolkien
content: Upon the hearth the fire is red, Beneath the roof there is a bed; But not yet weary are our feet, Still round the corner we may meet A sudden tree or standing stone That none have seen but we alone. Tree and flower and leaf and grass, Let them pass! Let them pass! Hill and water under sky, Pass them by! Pass them by! Still round the corner there may wait A new road or a secret gate, And though we pass them by today, Tomorrow we may come this way And take the hidden paths that run Towards the Moon or to the Sun. Apple, thorn, and nut and sloe, Let them go! Let them go! Sand and stone and pool and dell, Fare you well! Fare you well! Home is behind, the world ahead, And there are many paths to tread Through shadows to the edge of night, Until the stars are all alight. Then world behind and home ahead, We'll wander back to home and bed. Mist and twilight, cloud and shade, Away shall fade! Away shall fade! Fire and lamp, and meat and bread, And then to bed! And then to bed!

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a big horse. The horse was very special and looked different from other horses. It was unique! 

One day, a bad man came and tried to steal the horse. The farmer saw the bad man and shouted for help. The bad man ran away and the horse was safe. 

The farmer was happy that the horse was not stolen. He gave the horse some hay to eat and patted it on the head. The horse neighed happily and the farmer smiled. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy had a red bike with a wide seat. She loved to ride her bike up and down the street. One day, Amy decided she wanted to raise the handle on her bike so she could ride even better.

Amy asked her dad for help. Her dad got a tool and helped her raise the handle. Now, Amy could reach the handle easily and ride her bike even better. She was so happy.

Amy rode her bike up and down the wide street. She waved at her friends as she rode by. She was so proud of her bike with the raised handle. And from that day on, Amy had even more fun riding her bike.

One day, a little girl named Lucy got a letter in the mail. She was very excite. She opened the letter and read it out loud. It said, "Come to my party, please. Love, Tom."

Lucy went to the party. There were balloons and games. She saw her friend Tom. He said, "Hi, Lucy! I'm happy you're here."

At the party, they ate yummy cake. It was sweet and good. Lucy and Tom played and laughed. They had lots of fun. At the end of the day, Lucy went home with a big smile on her face.

One day, a man went to the park. The man was not happy. He was impatient. He wanted to see something fun. He sat on a bench and looked around.

Then, a big rabbit appeared. The rabbit was funny. The man and the rabbit played with a ball. They had a lot of fun. The rabbit made the man happy.

After some time, the rabbit had to go. The man was not impatient anymore. He had a good time with the rabbit. The man went home with a big smile.

Once upon a time, there was a kangaroo named Joey. Joey loved to jump and hop around in the forest. One day, he met a bird named Tweetie. Tweetie said, "Hi Joey, let's play a game!" Joey was excited and said, "What game?" Tweetie said, "Let's test who can jump higher!" Joey agreed and they started to jump.

Joey jumped and jumped, but he couldn't jump as high as Tweetie. He started to feel dizzy and fell down. Tweetie said, "Are you okay?" Joey said, "I'm dizzy." Tweetie said, "Let's stop playing and rest." Joey agreed and they sat down under a tree. They became friends and played other games together.

Once upon there was a little girl called Susie. Susie lived with her Mommy and Daddy in a nice warm house. Every day Susie would wander in the backyard. She would run around and pick the healthy flowers.

One sunny day Susie was playing in the backyard when a little bird flew down from the sky. The bird said, "Hello Susie, would you like to come on an adventure with me?" Susie replied, "Yes, I would love to!" 

Off they flew over the trees, the clouds, and the mountains. It was so fun! Susie learned a lot about birds and the world around her. 

Finally, Susie and the bird had to come back home. Susie thanked the bird for the wonderful adventure and waved goodbye. She returned back to her own backyard, happy and healthy.

Tread lightly, she is near Under the snow, Speak gently, she can hear The daisies grow. All her bright golden hair Tarnished with rust, She that was young and fair Fallen to dust. Lily-like, white as snow, She hardly knew She was a woman, so Sweetly she grew. Coffin-board, heavy stone, Lie on her breast, I vex my heart alone She is at rest. Peace, Peace, she cannot hear Lyre or sonnet, All my life's buried here, Heap earth upon it.

name_of_work: Music I Heard by Conrad Aiken
content: Music I heard with you was more than music, And bread I broke with you was more than bread; Now that I am without you, all is desolate; All that was once so beautiful is dead. Your hands once touched this table and this silver, And I have seen your fingers hold this glass. These things do not remember you, beloved, And yet your touch upon them will not pass. For it was in my heart that you moved among them, And blessed them with your hands and with your eyes; And in my heart they will remember always, --They knew you once, O beautiful and wise.

Jonny was helping his mom clean up the house. He was being very careful and thoughtful with the furniture. 

"What are you doing, mom?" asked Jonny. 

"I'm tidying up the living room," replied Mom. 

Suddenly, he saw a big chair that belonged to Grandpa. It was full of dust, but Jonny knew how much Grandpa cared about it. 

He looked at Mom, who was smiling. "Let's clean it up and make it nice for Grandpa," she said. 

So, Jonny and Mom cleaned up the chair and made it look shiny and new again. 

When Grandpa visited and saw his chair, he was so happy. He thanked them and said, "I can see how much you both care." Jonny smiled proudly. 

He was so glad that he and Mom were able to make Grandpa's chair look nice and thoughtul.

Manny was a brave little boy and he loved adventure. One day he decided to explore a nearby motor. He had never seen a motor before and he was curious to see what it looked like.

Manny cautiously approached the motor. It was bigger and scarier than he expected. He was a bit unsure, but he took a deep breath and decided to explore it.

Just then, he heard a crunching sound. He looked around and noticed a big bear was chewing on something near the wheel of the motor. Manny gasped and he was very scared. He wanted to run away, but he was too scared to move!

The bear noticed Manny and looked up. It said in a kind voice "Come here, little one. Don't be scared of me. I'm just chewing on some fruits."

Manny slowly moved closer and he felt a bit calmer when he saw the smile on the bear's face. Suddenly, the adventure didn't seem so scary after all.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was so happy. Her mommy and daddy loved her very much. 

Every day they would hug and kiss her. She would laugh and smile. She felt so happy when they kissed her. 

One day her mommy decided to give her a surprise. Her mommy gave her a pass. It was colorful! The little girl was so excited. She hugged and kissed her mommy. 

The pass was to go to the zoo. The little girl was so happy that she kept kissing and hugging her mommy. She couldn't wait to visit the zoo. 

The trip to the zoo was very fun and colorful. The little girl saw so many animals. She was so happy and she couldn't stop kissing and hugging her mommy and daddy. 

The little girl had the most wonderful day ever. She was so happy she couldn't stop smiling and kissing. 

The end!

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went on an adventure in the forest. He walked a long way, and his foot started to hurt. He saw an old man sitting on a rock, so he asked him for help. The old man said, "I have an ancient remedy for your foot. Come with me to my house, and I will fix it."

Timmy followed the old man to his house. He saw many interesting things, like a big book and a shiny sword. The old man gave Timmy a drink and rubbed his foot with a strange cream. Timmy felt much better and thanked the old man. "You're welcome," said the old man, "but before you go, I have a gift for you." He gave Timmy a magical stone and said, "This stone will protect you on your journey home."

Timmy was happy and said goodbye to the old man. He walked a little way and saw a big bear. He remembered the old man's gift and held the stone tightly. But the stone did not work, and the bear chased Timmy all the way home. Timmy was sad that the old man's gift did not protect him, and he wished he had never gone on the adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went for a walk in the forest with her mom. They saw a big tree with an original shape. 

"Mommy, look at that tree! It's so pretty!" said Lily.

"Yes, it is," said her mom. "But we must be careful not to wake the animals."

As they walked further, they saw a rabbit on the path. Lily wanted to touch it, but her mom said, "No, we must yield to the animals and let them be."

Lily learned that it's important to respect nature and all its creatures. She went home happy and told her dad all about her adventure in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane who loved to play. She always had a smile on her face and was full of energy. One day, Jane was playing with her toys in the dirt when suddenly her mother urged her to come inside. 

"But why, mommy?" Jane asked. 

"It's getting late and it's time for dinner," her mother replied.

Jane put down her toys and walked to her mother, putting her hand on her mother's shoulder. They made their way over to the house, but when they got to the door, Jane's mom stopped.

"Oh no! Look at your hands, Jane," she said.

Sure enough, Jane's hands were very dirty! Her mother urged her to go to the faucet to wash up before they went inside. Jane smiled and did as her mother said. Now her hands were much cleaner and they went inside for dinner. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a red dog named Spot. Spot loved to play in the mud. One day, Spot got very dirty. His fur was full of mud and dirt. Spot's mom saw him and said, "Spot, you need a bath."

Spot's mom filled a big tub with warm water. She got the shampoo and started to wash Spot's red fur. Spot did not believe that the shampoo would make him clean. But as his mom washed him, the dirt and mud started to go away.

Soon, Spot's red fur was clean and shiny again. He looked in the mirror and saw how nice he looked. Spot now believed that shampoo could make him clean. He promised his mom that he would try to stay clean and not play in the mud so much. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there were two sisters named Molly and Penny. Molly was the oldest, and she was very wise beyond her years. 

One day, Molly wanted to teach Penny a lesson about being kind, so she asked Penny if she wanted to marry a smooth stone. Penny thought this sounded like a strange idea, but wanted to be nice to her big sister, so she agreed. 

Molly took a smooth stone from the ground and held it in both hands. She told Penny to place her hands together over the top of the stone and say a special phrase. When Penny repeated the phrase, the stone became joined to her hands, just like a ring when two people get married. 

Penny smiled, feeling excited, and thanked Molly. Then Molly said, â€œThe lesson here is that when we are kind and understanding to one another, and treat each other with love and respect, then our bond will become even stronger and our relationship will be smooth like this stone.â€ 

Molly and Penny smiled happily and hugged each other tightly. From then on, they both remembered that no matter what, they would always have each otherâ€™s backs and show love and kindness.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily's mommy told her to go upstairs and get her favorite toy. So Lily went upstairs to get it. 

When she got there, she saw a bright light coming from her parents' room. She went to see what it was and found her mommy and daddy arguing. They were shouting and not listening to each other. 

Lily didn't know what to do, but she knew she had to tell someone. She ran downstairs to her neighbor's house and told them what she saw. The neighbor called the police and they came to help. 

In the end, Lily's mommy and daddy were taken away and Lily had to live with her grandma. It was a sad ending, but Lily knew she did the right thing by telling someone.

name_of_work: On Sitting Down to Read King Lear Once Again by John Keats
content: O golden-tongued Romance with serene lute! Fair plumed Syren! Queen of far away! Leave melodizing on this wintry day, Shut up thine olden pages, and be mute: Adieu! for once again the fierce dispute, Betwixt damnation and impassion'd clay Must I burn through; once more humbly assay The bitter-sweet of this Shakespearian fruit. Chief Poet! and ye clouds of Albion, Begetters of our deep eternal theme, When through the old oak forest I am gone, Let me not wander in a barren dream, But when I am consumed in the fire, Give me new Phoenix wings to fly at my desire.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved her blanket very much. She carried it everywhere she went. One day, Lily was playing with her toys when her big brother came in the room. He wanted to scare her, so he hid behind the door and jumped out. 

"Boo!" he shouted. 

Lily was so scared that she dropped her blanket and ran out of the room. Her brother picked up the blanket and laughed. "Ha ha, you're so foolish to be scared of me," he said. 

Lily was sad because she didn't have her blanket anymore. She went to bed that night without it and had a bad dream. The next morning, she woke up and found that her blanket was gone. Her brother had hidden it somewhere and she couldn't find it. Lily was so upset that she cried and cried. 

From that day on, Lily never trusted her brother again. She learned that it's not nice to scare people and take things that don't belong to you. She missed her blanket very much, but she knew that her brother would never give it back.

Harry was a curious three-year-old boy. He was looking around the house for something to do. His parents said he wanted to explore. So he did. 

Harry walked into the kitchen and stopped in front of the refrigerator. It was big, really huge. He wanted to try and open it. But it was too high for him to reach.

"Mom, can you help me open the enormous refrigerator?" he asked. 

His mom walked over. She said, "No problem. Let me help you."

She tried opening the door, but it wouldn't open. She turned the knob harder, but it still wouldn't open. Then she said, "It looks like the door is stuck. Let's keep trying."

So they tried together, and it opened! Harry was so happy. He saw shelves full of all his favorite food. He reached out and grabbed a container of juice.

"Thanks, Mom!" he said, happily.

Harry had discovered a great challenge. All he needed was a little help from his mom, and together they had found success.

Anna and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They used pots and pans and spoons and bowls. They also used water from the faucet to fill the pots and wash the dishes.

"Look, Anna, I made soup!" Ben said, holding a pot with water and some carrots and peas. "Do you want some?"

"Yes, please!" Anna said, smiling. She took a bowl and a spoon and waited for Ben to pour some soup for her.

But when Ben turned the faucet to get more water, something funny happened. The water came out very fast and very loud. It splashed all over Ben and Anna and the kitchen floor. Ben and Anna were wet and shocked.

"Surprise!" they heard a voice say. They looked up and saw their dad standing by the faucet. He had a big grin on his face. He had turned a knob that made the water come out stronger. He thought it would be a fun joke.

"Dad!" Ben and Anna said together. They were not happy. They did not like the surprise. They felt cold and wet and messy.

"I'm sorry, kids. I didn't mean to scare you. I just wanted to make you laugh," their dad said. He turned off the faucet and got some towels. He dried Ben and Anna and hugged them. "You were doing such a good job playing chefs. I'm very proud of you."

Ben and Anna felt a little better. They knew their dad loved them and was sorry. They hugged him back and said they loved him too. They decided to finish their soup and share it with their dad. They also decided to surprise him later with a big pie. But they would not use the faucet.
